name: Kagemaru Himeno
bio: Kagemaru Himeno (Japanese: 姫野かげまる), born July 24, 1972 in Kanagawa Prefecture, is a writer and illustrator who has provided material for Pokémon since the early years of the franchise. She started doing manga illustrations for RIBON Original in 1994, a magazine published by Shueisha, who along with other publishers Hakusensh and Shogakukan, own VIZ Media, which publishes manga outside Japan. Since 1997, Himeno has done many illustrations for Pokémon-related publications, including Pokémon Tales and her own series How I Became a Pokémon Card. She is also one of the few illustrators that has continued to produce card art since the early years of the Pokémon Trading Card Game. She likes to go by the nickname "Himemaru" (ヒメマル). Himeno's artwork has been featured on cards since the Jungle expansion, and as such, it is usually instantly recognizable to long-time followers of the TCG. She openly admits that she loves the paintings she does, which reflects in the quality of her art. Himeno uses watercolors and often uses bright and vivid colors with softer tones to highlight areas of light and shadow. She also adds soft white flecks on some her images, which could be interpreted as cotton spores or the like. These are particularly apparent on her older works. Over the years, she has developed a sharper eye for detail, resulting in more crisp images with more adventurous backgrounds.

name: Midori Harada
bio: Midori Harada (Japanese: 原田みどり Harada Midori) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. She has done work for various Pokémon materials and merchandise since 1996, but began illustrating cards for the TCG later in the series, starting with Cubone, Eevee, and Houndour from the Aquapolis expansion. She is known for her style, called Aire Verte, of calm European landscapes. This is carried over for the official Hoenn, Battle Frontier, Sinnoh, Battle Frontier, and updated Kanto and Johto maps seen in guidebooks.
trivia: Harada's favorite Pokémon is Cubone.

name: Atsuko Nishida
bio: Atsuko Nishida (Japanese: 西田敦子 / にしだあつこ Nishida Atsuko) is a graphic artist who has been involved with several aspects of the Pokémon franchise since it began. She was part of the graphics team on Pulseman, one of Game Freak's most successful early titles, working alongside Pokémon creator Satoshi Tajiri and artist Ken Sugimori. During the development of the first Pokémon games, she helped design key characters and several Pokémon, notably the cuter ones as opposed to the tougher ones. Nishida is a character designer for the mascot of the Pokémon franchise, Pikachu. She stated that first design of Pikachu looked like a vertically long daifuku rice confection with ears.[1] She also modeled Pikachu's cheeks, which are used to store electricity, after squirrels storing food in their cheeks.[2] Nishida is also a fan of Eevee and the Eeveelutions, having personally designed almost all of the Eeveelutions, with the exception of Jolteon and Flareon.[3][4] She also contributed to the conceptual design of characters that appeared in the first few Pokémon movies, as well as several of the main cast members of Pokémon the Series itself, including Ash Ketchum, Misty, and Brock.[5] Nishida has continued to work within many areas of the franchise, credited on the majority of the core series games and movies, and has produced an array of original illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. She is also the illustrator for the mini-comic series titled Together with Pokémon! (Japanese: ポケモンといっしょ！) for a monthly children's magazine, Chara Pafe (Japanese: キャラぱふぇ).
trivia: Atsuko Nishida is the only person who has been credited as a Pokémon designer in every generation.

In an interview with the character designers of Pokémon in 2018, Nishida said that Pikachu was supposed to have a third evolution stage after Raichu, which was named "Gorochu" (Japanese: ゴロチュウ). Ken Sugimori stated that it was scrapped for game balance reasons.[6]
Nishida's favorite Pokémon is Charizard.[6]

name: Kouki Saitou
bio: Kouki Saitou (Japanese: 斉藤コーキ Saitō Kōki), born May 13, 1973, is a freelance illustrator who does work for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Prior to this, he numerous manga illustrations for popular Japanese game tie-ins under his ¼ King! label. He has also designed a number of characters and mascots that feature on his website as part of a fantasy land called "Kortlek", which showcase his quirky yet detailed drawing style. He has cited Dragon Ball creator Akira Toriyama and anime directed by Hayao Miyazaki as some of his biggest influences.[2][3]

name: Masakazu Fukuda
bio:
Masakazu Fukuda (Japanese: 福田正和) is an illustrator who was primarily involved with character and graphic design with many game companies in the 1990s before becoming a freelance illustrator. He has been providing artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game since 2003.
Fukuda holds many artists in high regard and has several interests. He is a fan of mecha and admires the work of designer Hajime Katoki. Other favorites include manga artists Katsuhiro Otomo, Masamune Shirow and Akira Toriyama, as well as illustrators Jun Suemi and Takani Yoshiyuki, who designed the package art for many military model kits in the 1960s. He is a keen biker, engages in wide-angle photography, and enjoys electronic music and music from the late 60s, particularly that of James Brown.

name: Sekio
bio: Sekio (Japanese: せきお) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Murkrow from the Guardians Rising expansion.

name: Yusuke Ishikawa
bio: Yusuke Ishikawa is an illustrator of some Pokémon TCG cards.

name: Hajime Kusajima
bio: Hajime Kusajima (Japanese: 草嶋一) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Kusajima's first cards were Karen's Pokémon from the Japanese Pokémon VS expansion. His first English cards released in the Expedition Base Set expansion. Over the years, he has changed his style several times. During the e-Card Series, Kusajima's method consisted of watercolor and ink, but he also used varying intensities depending on the Pokémon portrayed. In some cases he used light tones with thin outlines, but for more dominant images, switched to deeper colors with heavier brushstrokes and thicker outlines. During the early EX Series, he switched to a more computer-aided style with solid colors and tone highlights that gave an almost cartoon-like appearance. It was also during this time that he began to use often very colorful or detailed backgrounds in order to create contrast. Towards the end of the EX Series, he expanded on this style by using much heavier outlines, larger areas of shadow and more vivid colors while also experimenting with his original style to produce soft and realistic images by effectively using light and shadow. He would not illustrate any other cards until the Stormfront expansion, where he again demonstrated the variety of his coloring techniques over the coming sets. Some featured plainly colored images and others with varying brushstroke effects, while some featured extremely deep colors and areas of shadow, as well as the complete opposite with images highlighted with intense light. Kusajima stopped contributing new artwork to the TCG around the beginning of the Sun & Moon Series.

name: Naoyo Kimura
bio: Naoyo Kimura (Japanese: 木村(きむら)直代(なおよ) Kimura Naoyo; born 1960[1]) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His first cards were Seel, Zapdos, and Graveler from the Japanese Expansion Sheet Series 2. His first cards released in English were the Wizards Black Star Promos Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres released alongside The Power of One. He is notable for creating illustrations for the Neo Series and the Southern Islands promotional set. Besides contributing artwork for the Pokémon TCG, Naoyo Kimura illustrated the Pokémon Tales picture book Come Out, Squirtle! For the 2023 "Pokémon x Van Gogh" art collaboration, Kimura contributed illustrations of Pikachu and the evolutionary lines of Honchkrow and Corviknight, inspired by Vincent van Gogh's Self-Portrait with Grey Felt Hat and Wheatfield with Crows, respectively.

name: Pokemon Rumble
bio: Pokémon Rumble (Japanese: 乱戦！ポケモンスクランブル Melee! Pokémon Scramble) is a WiiWare game, and the first game in the Pokémon Rumble series. It was released in Japan on June 16, 2009, November 16 for North America, and in Europe four days afterwards. It could be purchased for 1,500 Wii Points. This title is no longer purchasable as of the Wii Shop Channel's shutdown on January 31, 2019.
trivia: A prototype for North America was shown at the Wizard World's Big Apple Comic Con in October 2009.[citation needed]

name: Shin-ichi Yoshida
bio: Shin-ichi Yoshida (Japanese: 吉田振一) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Ken Sugimori
bio: Ken Sugimori (Japanese: 杉森建 Sugimori Ken; born January 27, 1966) is a friend of Satoshi Tajiri and illustrator of the original artwork for Pokémon games. He also has developed conceptual artwork for the movies, and illustrates TCG cards and merchandising. The original artwork for all 151 Generation I Pokémon was done by Ken Sugimori.[1] In Pokémon Red and Green, the in-game sprites were initially drawn by various artists. Sugimori later redrew each Pokémon in watercolor for promotional use. While doing so, he revised and refined many elements, which ultimately shaped how the designs were perceived by the public[2], with potential examples being Pikachu, Vaporeon, Dragonite, and Mew. Sugimori's change of style over the years has been noticeable. Initially, he used a stiff, lightly shaded style using watercolors that was very reminiscent of Akira Toriyama's visual style, particularly that from 1989 onward. However, his now digitally-produced drawings of people and creatures have gradually gained more muscle definition, significantly rounder corners, heavier shading, and more natural and fluid poses.
trivia:
The character Kenji from Pokémon the Series (known as Tracey Sketchit in the English dub) may be a homage to Ken Sugimori, especially as both enjoy creating art. This is similar to the way Satoshi, known as Ash Ketchum in the English dub, is named after Satoshi Tajiri.
Similarly, one of the default rival names in Pokémon LeafGreen Version is Ken (Japanese: ケン Ken), an allusion to Sugimori.

name: Naoki Saito
bio: Naoki Saito (Japanese: さいとうなおき Saitō Naoki, real name in kanji 齋藤直葵, born 1982 in Yamagata, Japan[1]) is a digital illustrator who has provided art for the Pokémon Trading Card Game since the HeartGold & SoulSilver expansion, as well as art for a couple of Pokémon games. Saito is a graduate of Tama Art University and previously worked at Konami Digital Entertainment Co., Ltd. before becoming freelance.[citation needed] In addition to the Pokémon TCG, he has also provided illustrations for several other trading card franchises: Duel Masters,[citation needed] Monster Hunter,[citation needed] Juushinden: Ultimate Beast Battlers,[citation needed] and Eternal Wheel.[citation needed] Saito's style is vibrant and surreal, and often juxtaposes or merges the organic with the geometric. He also puts emphasis on texture to give subjects character. His work within the TCG is similar but subtler, instead using highlights and contrasting colors to make Pokémon stand out. In addition to card illustrations, Saito provided the packaging art for the Garchomp and Hydreigon Half Decks[2] and the box art for Everyone's Exciting Battle.[citation needed] He also illustrated the Pokémon Tales book Crustle's Moving,[citation needed] available to read on the Pokémon Daisuki Club website.

name: Sumiyoshi Kizuki
bio: Sumiyoshi Kizuki (Japanese: 木月(きづき)すみよし; born 1967[2]) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Her style was often notable for a soft crayon-like look, with her art initially being featured in the Team Rocket expansion.

name: Mitsuhiro Arita
bio: Mitsuhiro Arita (Japanese: 有田満弘), born January 12, 1970 in Fukuoka Prefecture, is a freelance illustrator who has been providing artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game since its inception. In addition to Pokémon, he has also provided artwork for several other trading or collectible card games based on franchises such as Shin Megami Tensei, Monster Hunter, and Super Sentai. He has provided many illustrations for Final Fantasy XI online content, as well as producing written articles, featured works, and cover art across numerous publications. He likes to paint pictures while he travels, a hobby he calls "Mobile Painting," which he began doing while using a Pocket PC.[2] Arita is completely self-taught in his artistry.[3]
trivia: Arita has a degree in Electrical and Software engineering.
Arita's favorite Pokémon is Mewtwo.[13][14]

name: Kazuyuki Kano
bio: Kazuyuki Kano is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Kyoko Umemoto
bio: Kyoko Umemoto (Japanese: 梅本(うめもと)恭子(きょうこ)) is a freelance illustrator[1] who began their work on the series as an illustrator on the Pokémon Trading Card Game, the first of which was Arbok from the Expedition Base Set expansion.

name: Ryo Ueda
bio: Ryo Ueda (Japanese: 植田亮) is a 3D illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Following the development of 3D software and the death of the game's original 3D artist Keiji Kinebuchi, Ryo Ueda became one of the TCG's prominent 3D artists. His first cards were Chansey ex, Scyther ex, and Sneasel ex from the EX Ruby & Sapphire expansion. He would go on to provide many illustrations for Trainer cards and high-rarity Pokémon such as Pokémon-ex, Pokémon LV.X, and Full Art Pokémon-EX. During the Sun & Moon and Sword & Shield Series, Ueda also contributed various gold etched Secret cards. Many of the Pokémon he has portrayed are powerful variants within the game, therefore Ueda creates solid renders and plays with lighting and elemental image effects, such as fire or lightning to often give the Pokémon a dominant presence. For non-Pokémon card images, he usually creates the item or location in the foreground and develops an accompanying background or environment to fit the purpose.

name: Daisuke Ito
bio: Daisuke Ito is an illustrator who contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game during the Diamond & Pearl Series. Ito has illustrated 43 cards, the first of which was Palkia, one of the DP-P Promotional cards. A full list of cards illustrated by Daisuke Ito can be found here.

name: Motofumi Fujiwara
bio: Motofumi Fujiwara (Fuziwara also seen; Japanese: 藤原基史 Fujiwara Motofumi) is a freelance designer and former key member at GAME FREAK until September 2013. He has also illustrated several cards for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: kawayoo
bio: Kawaguchi Yoohei (Japanese: 川口洋平), born 1974, is a freelance digital illustrator who has provided artwork for the Pokémon series. He began work with the Pokémon Trading Card Game, illustrating the Walrein, Hippopotas, and Nidorino included in the Rising Rivals expansion. He is often credited by his nickname "kawayoo" (川洋) in his work. Youhei's style is very distinctive, brought about from his creative approach and dedication to each one of his illustrations. He creates subjects from scratch by using a graphic tablet in image editing software and applying hundreds of strokes to define base shapes, outlines, backgrounds and final details. These result in often surreal, heavy, multi-layered images reminiscent of oil paintings. His images often focus on muscle tone, expression or contrast and have themes influenced by cyberpunk or anime. The Pokémon he has portrayed are often very detailed, vibrant and in dynamic positions, among which include the Pokémon  cards, which he provided all the artwork for (with the exception of LV.X variants). Youhei drew the promotional artwork, which includes booster pack art and theme deck art, for every expansion in the HeartGold & SoulSilver series. Outside the TCG, he illustrated maps and other promotional artwork for Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire and every Generation VII core series game.

name: Shibuzoh.
bio: Shibuzoh. (Japanese: しぶぞー Shibuzō) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Clefairy from the Generations expansion.

name: Hisao Nakamura
bio: Hisao Nakamura is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His first cards were Jynx and Drowzee from the Aquapolis expansion, and he continued to illustrate cards up to the EX Dragon Frontiers expansion.

name: Satoshi Shirai
bio: Satoshi Shirai (Japanese: しらいさとし), born October 5, is a freelance 3D CG illustrator who was first commissioned to provide artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game in 2012. His first cards were Blastoise and Musharna from the Boundaries Crossed expansion. Shirai's work for the TCG was his first professional contract after graduating from Kyoto Seika University studying digital creation. While studying his course, he uploaded many of his projects to his personal blog, to deviantART, and to YouTube, showcasing his approach to the creation, design, and animation of numerous original and quirky characters. Several of these characters evolved into subjects portrayed in Lolipop Melancholy, a 3D web comic used in his graduation exhibition.

name: tetsuya koizumi
bio: Scav (born February 22, 1981[1] in Shiga, Japan[2]), formerly credited under the name tetsuya koizumi (Japanese: 小泉(こいずみ)哲哉(てつや))[3], is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His first card was Tangrowth from the Burning Shadows expansion, and his name was changed to Scav beginning with Rapid Strike Urshifu VMAX from the Brilliant Stars expansion.

name: Keiko Fukuyama
bio: Keiko Fukuyama (Japanese: ふくやまけいこ), whose original name is 福山慶子,  born September 7, 1961, Tokyo, is a freelance artist who has provided illustrations for numerous manga publications and light novels, many of which she has authored, as well as delving into animation. Her debut work, Fukuyama Jikkuvukku, was self-published in 1981. Fukuyama's style involves the use of traditional mediums, including felt pens and pencils to create vibrant, colorful images. She has written and illustrated a handful of Pokémon-related books, and also provided a number of illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game in 1999 and 2002, most notably Pokémon featured in the Rainbow Island aspect of the Southern Islands Collection. For a list of cards illustrated by Keiko Fukuyama, go here.

name: Nakaoka
bio: Nakaoka is an illustrator who contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game during the EX and Diamond & Pearl Series. In total, Nakaoka illustrated 48 cards (excluding reprints), starting with four cards in the EX Team Magma vs Team Aqua expansion. Their final illustrations were featured in the Diamond & Pearl expansion. A full list of cards illustrated by Nakaoka can be found here.

name: sui
bio: sui (Japanese: 彗) is a freelance digital illustrator who provides original illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, with her work debuting in the Arceus expansion. She has also produced an array of illustrations featured in a number of publications, such as guidebooks and CD covers. Sui specializes in depicting fantasy-scenes and animals, and includes animals and gaming among her interests. She particularly likes producing images that have a sense of motion. Sui also indulges in fan-art, which feature characters from many established Nintendo franchises. sui uses a graphics tablet and a number of image editing software suites for her illustrations, which are created in an airbrush style. She uses areas of highly saturated color and luminosity in her work, resulting in vibrant, atmospheric, and serene images. Light is emphasized in almost all of her original work. Environments often incorporate elements of nature, as well as animals.

name: PLANETA Mochizuki
bio: Juukou Mochizuki (born December 3, 1997)[2] is an illustrator at PLANETA who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. They are credited as PLANETA Mochizuki on cards they have illustrated, the first of which was Gardevoir V from the Japanese Explosive Walker expansion. Their first cards released in English were Mew V and Crobat V from the Darkness Ablaze expansion.

name: MAHOU
bio: MAHOU (Japanese: まほう) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His first cards were Sentret and Furret from the HeartGold & SoulSilver expansion.

name: Kanako Eo
bio: Kanako Eo (Japanese: 江尾可奈子) is a graphic designer and has been an employee of Game Freak since at least 2002, contributing to the graphic and Pokémon design in the majority of main series Pokémon games during her time there. She has been involved with the conceptual design of characters in several Pokémon movies (credited as Kanako Eoh in some), and she also illustrated Mysterious Pirate Ship, a Pokémon Tales book available to read on the Pokémon Daisuki Club website. Kanako Eo has produced many original illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, beginning with Shroomish from the EX Deoxys expansion.

name: Yumi
bio: Yumi (Japanese: ユミ) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, who has been illustrating since Steam Siege starting with Pyroar.

name: Hironobu Yoshida
bio: Hironobu Yoshida (Japanese: 吉田宏信; born 1972[1]) is a graphic designer who has been involved with several aspects of the Pokémon franchise for many years. Since Pokémon Yellow in 1997, Yoshida has had a hand in the development of the majority of main series Pokémon games, both as a graphic and Pokémon designer. He is credited in several of the Pokémon movies within the character design department and has illustrated a handful of cards for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. He also designed the main art for the World Championships since 2007. The Pokémon he is known to have designed include Wobbuffet, Dunsparce, and several Legendary and Mythical Pokémon such as Celebi, Rayquaza, Deoxys, and Darkrai.[2] Additionally, he created an array of unique characters and lent his voice to some of them for the Game Boy Advance game Drill Dozer, another Game Freak title directed by fellow Pokémon designer Ken Sugimori in 2005. He has also branched into other media, performing a live-action version of the Poké Dude Show (an in-game tutorial featured in Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen), dressing up as Primo, the Poké Dude, and giving advice on how to do various things in the Pokémon games. He reprises this role in the song Teach Me, Poké Dude!, in which he engages a group of children in the same manner as the in-game character and provides the main vocals.

name: 5ban Graphics
bio: 5ban Graphics is a group of artists within Creatures, Inc. who have illustrated many cards for the Pokémon Trading Card Game from Black & White onward. The group has designed many Trainer Cards, as well as many Full Art cards and Pokémon cards for the Black and White, XY, Sun & Moon, Sword & Shield, and Scarlet & Violet TCG Series. In 2012, a brief interview about the creation of card artwork was posted on the Creatures, Inc. PTCG blog in which they state they like to make the Pokémon look 3D along with exemplifying the best qualities of the Pokémon when possible so they stand out on their own. The group's name is a reference to Creatures' former address at 10 Gobancho, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo.[citation needed]

name: Lee HyunJung
bio: Lee HyunJung (Hyunjung Lee also seen; Korean: 이현정; Japanese: 李ヒョンジョン; born on February 27, Daegu) is a Korean former designer senior artist at GAME FREAK between April 2006 until December 2018, as well as an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, with her first contribution being Shinx from the Mysterious Treasures expansion. From January 2019, HyunJung began work as a freelance character artist, where she continues to illustrate for Pokémon.

name: Keiji Kinebuchi
bio: Keiji Kinebuchi (Japanese: 杵淵敬二; born February 14, 1956[1] – c.2002[2]) was a 3D illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. When the TCG was first released, Kinebuchi was one of the few 3D artists, making his art for the first few expansions instantly recognizable. Due to limitations of 3D software at the time, many of the Pokémon he created images for were composed of very simple shapes, consisting of basic textures and lighting effects. He was known for creating the art for the majority of early Trainer cards, and as the TCG continued, he worked on Trainer card art almost exclusively. He had invited Mitsuhiro Arita to join the project.[3] Kinebuchi's last illustrations were featured in the Aquapolis expansion, during which time other 3D illustrators were beginning to contribute with more sophisticated images. He was credited as the illustrator for all Basic Energy cards, as well as a few Special Energy cards up until the Expedition Base Set, where there was a major change in the card layout. Mitsuhiro Arita designed the Energy symbols on the cards, whereas Kinebuchi designed the Energy cards' layouts.[3] Kinebuchi is also credited as an illustrator for some of the Trainer cards in the Pokémon Trading Figure Game; however, all of the images are taken from work he had previously done for the TCG. In total, Kinebuchi illustrated 106 cards, excluding reprints. For a list of cards he has illustrated, go here.

name: Shin Nagasawa
bio: Shin Nagasawa (Japanese: 長澤(ながさわ)真(しん)) is a freelance illustrator who provides artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game and other Pokémon related merchandise. Nagasawa worked as a graphic designer at Square for a number of years after graduating from university in 1994, and was credited as a monster concept artist for several titles during this time. He went freelance in 2000, and has had numerous illustrations and manga series published since, as well as continuing to provide concept art for several games and illustrations for various trading card games. He often uses the pseudonym "JASON" (ジェイソン) or "J-mura" (J村) for self-published works (dōjinshi). Nagasawa's first illustrations were featured Dragonite FB and Regigigas FB from the Supreme Victors expansion. In addition to card art, he has also produced the packaging artwork for expansions released outside of Japan, which include Boundaries Crossed, Plasma Storm, Plasma Freeze, and Plasma Blast. Other Pokémon related illustrations include those featured on merchandise sold in Japan. These include: Reshiram & Zekrom 2011 New Year's Greeting card and Pochi bags, Tepig, Pignite, and Emboar Uniqlo T-shirt design, Kyurem VS Tornadus•Thundurus•Landorus Pokémon Center stationery, and Gardevoir & Lilligant deck shields. Nagasawa's illustration style within the TCG varies as does his work for other publications. Some are drawn in a style reminiscent of comic books, in that the Pokémon is drawn with a solid black outline, with areas of extreme shadow and other details also in solid black. In other illustrations, color shading is used to define details and the accompanying background, making outlines less explicit. In nearly all instances Nagasawa focuses on motion and a specific portion of the Pokémon's body with varying degrees of tilt, giving the impression that the Pokémon is moving out of the confines of the image.

name: Kyoko Koizumi
bio: Kyoko Koizumi is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Yuka Morii
bio: Yuka Morii (Japanese: 森井(もりい)ユカ) is a professional clay modeler who has provided illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. She is a graduate of Tokyo Zokei University and earned a MA degree in Living Design at the Kuwasawa Design Institute. In addition to her work for the TCG she has also designed mascots for various companies, published several art & culture books, provided artwork for other publications and is a part-time lecturer of illustration at the Kuwasawa Design Institute.

name: kirisAki
bio: kirisAki (Japanese: きりさき; born February 5th[1]) is an artist that has participated in a variety of official Pokémon releases as a key artist, such as Pokémon Masters EX, and a Holowear designer on Pokémon UNITE. She is also an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, starting with Tangela from the Legendary Treasures expansion.

name: SATOSHI NAKAI
bio: SATOSHI NAKAI (Japanese: 仲井さとし Nakai Satoshi) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Whirlipede from the Burning Shadows expansion.

name: Aya Kusube
bio: Aya Kusube (Japanese: 楠部文 Kusube Aya), born 1966, Saitama Prefecture, is a freelance illustrator. She primarily illustrates books and magazines, as well as advertising material aimed at children, using her own drawing style which mirrors that of children’s drawings. She was also involved as a conceptual designer for the famous Doraemon franchise. Kusube has been involved with the Pokémon franchise since 1998, writing and illustrating a number of Pokémon Tales books, and moving on to produce many illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.
trivia: Her late father, Daikichirou Kusube, was the president and founder of the Shin-Ei Animation Company, which produces many popular anime series in Japan. Her brother Takumi, who also works for Shin-Ei, is a CG animator and lyricist, and was similarly involved with developing the re-envisioned Doraemon franchise.

name: K. Utsunomiya
bio: Kiyoshi Utsunomiya is a 3D graphic designer who worked for Creatures, Inc. He has provided illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, credited as K. Utsunomiya.

name: Wataru Kawahara
bio: Wataru Kawahara is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His illustrations premiered in the Beat of the Frontier expansion and its deck kit. The cards he illustrated include Cyrus's main Pokémon in the deck kit, Charizard G LV.X, as well as a couple Trainer cards in the main expansion. So far, he has illustrated 36 cards for the trading card game. For a list of cards he illustrated, go here. He was also credited for working on games such as Tales of Symphonia and Sonic and The Secret Rings.

name: PLANETA Igarashi
bio: Kazuya Igarashi is an illustrator who has worked at PLANETA since 2011.[1] He has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game, credited as PLANETA Igarashi on cards he has illustrated. His first card was Full Art Ultra Necrozma-GX from the Forbidden Light expansion.

name: Eske Yoshinob
bio: Eske Yoshinob is a freelance illustrator and programmer who has provided work for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Originally a game model designer working for Now Production, he later moved on to producing 3D CG material for Daiichi Sankyo before becoming employed at Square Visual Works, part of Square Enix, in 2005. While there he was involved setup simulation, pipeline tool development, and model creation/animation for games in the Final Fantasy series and the Kingdom Hearts series. Concurrently, he also worked at Exit Tunes, Inc., then called Quake Holdings, as an illustrator, primarily involved in the production of album covers for the Exit Trance series. He chose to go freelance at the end of 2009. In 2010, he provided 3D model and animation work while at Polygon Pictures, and was involved in the development of Transformers Prime and Tron: Uprising. He began producing illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game in 2011, and began providing workflow and pipeline solutions for Toei Animation in 2012.

name: Katsura Tabata
bio: Katsura Tabata is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Toshinao Aoki
bio: Toshinao Aoki (Japanese: 青木俊直 Aoki Toshinao) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His first card, Surfing Pikachu, was released for the Japan Railways Group Train Rally in August of 1997, and sporadically contributed to the TCG, up to and including EX FireRed & LeafGreen expansion. In the Rising Rivals and Supreme Victors expansions, a few of his illustrations were featured as the retro cards. Then, after a nearly 19 year absence, Toshinao Aoki returned to the TCG to illustrate Exeggutor for Crown Zenith, and has once again become a recurring illustrator. In addition to Pokémon cards, his artwork was featured in the Pokémon Tales story books Pikachu's Day, Lapras Makes a Friend, I'm Not Pikachu, and Wake Up, Lugia!. In total, Aoki illustrated 61 cards for the trading card game. For a list of cards he illustrated, go here.

name: Mina Nakai
bio: Mina Nakai (Japanese: ナカイミナ, 中井美菜 Nakai Mina) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Machop from the Generations expansion.

name: Ayaka Yoshida
bio: Ayaka Yoshida (Japanese: ヨシダアヤカ Yoshida Ayaka) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Suicune from the Call of Legends expansion. Ayaka Yoshida is also a former member of 5ban Graphics, as mentioned in her Twitter bio.

name: Miki Tanaka
bio: Miki Tanaka (Japanese: 田中未樹 Tanaka Miki; born September 22) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Her first card was Slowpoke from the Fossil expansion. Miki Tanaka's artwork is very recognizable due to her simplistic style, which involves little variation of shades, and there is hardly ever any line art around the subject.
trivia: Tanaka has two children, as mentioned in her Twitter bio.

name: Shin-ichi Yoshikawa
bio: Shin-ichi Yoshikawa is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: CR CG gangs
bio: CR CG gangs is a group of artists which make illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. So far, they have illustrated 55 cards for the TCG, the majority of which were released during the "Neo" sets, mostly consisting of Trainer cards and Unown. For a full list of cards illustrated by CR CG gangs, look here.

name: Suwama Chiaki
bio: Suwama Chiaki (Japanese: 諏訪間(すわま)千晃(ちあき)) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Her very first illustrations were used in the PLAY Promotional card collection, all of which were used on cards given to players upon their 4th Season Subscription into the Pokémon Players Club. Her first illustration released in English was Combusken from the EX Crystal Guardians expansion. Although Chiaki was a consistent contributor to the TCG for years, she has not illustrated a new card since the Vivid Voltage expansion. The style of her illustrations often uses soft shading and light colors, which is very similar to that of Atsuko Nishida.

name: Takabon
bio: Takabon is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: TOKIYA
bio: Tokiya Sakuba (Japanese: 作場季野), often credited as simply TOKIYA (トキヤ), is a freelance digital illustrator who has provided art for the Pokémon Trading Card Game since the Arceus expansion. She was born in 1983 in Tokyo, Japan. Her style is very similar to that of kawayoo, utilizing a graphic tablet in image editing software to create base outlines, shapes and final details culminating in complex and atmospheric images. Her art focuses on insects, mechanics and the human body resulting in often very surreal images – some of which are quite extreme compared to similar artists, featuring elements of nudity and graphic violence. The Pokémon she has portrayed, as well as their environment, are very detailed and have surreal qualities. Thus far, TOKIYA has illustrated 91 cards for the Pokémon TCG (excluding reprints). For a list of cards she has illustrated, go here.
trivia: In addition to TOKIYA, she is also sometimes known as ARMA-EATER (アルマイーター), which was also the name of her first website. Another alias and the name of her current site is her family name backwards (Abukas).

name: sowsow
bio: sowsow (born 1988[1]) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His first cards were Avalugg, Inkay, and Cubone from the Forbidden Light expansion. Besides contributing artwork for the Pokémon TCG, sowsow has also contributed illustrations for Pokémon Sleep. For the 2023 "Pokémon x Van Gogh" art collaboration, sowsow contributed illustrations of Snorlax and Eevee, inspired by Vincent van Gogh's The Bedroom and Self-Portrait with Straw Hat, respectively.

name: Akira Komayama
bio: Akira Komayama (Japanese: こまやま明(あきら) Komayama Akira; born September 15, 1981)[1] is a illustrator who started in freelance in 2009[2] and has been contributing illustrations to the Pokémon Trading Card Game since 2010.[3] Komoyama's first card was BW-P Promotional Pansage. Their first cards released in English were Magby and Eevee from the Call of Legends expansion.

name: Eri Yamaki
bio: Eri Yamaki (Japanese: やまきえり Yamaki Eri) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Doduo from the Generations expansion.

name: Keiko Moritsugu
bio: Keiko Moritsugu (Japanese: 森次慶子 Moritsugu Keiko; born January 7, 1985) is an artist and painter who has worked for the Pokémon video game series and Trading Card Game. While working under Game Freak, she created multiple designs for Pokémon and the character N.[1] Moritsugu's first known involvement with the Pokémon franchise was in the staff of Pokémon Platinum under "Special Thanks", although it is currently unknown exactly what role she played in the development of that game. She later illustrated a card in the Arceus expansion: Heatran. In the staff of Pokémon Black and White, she is listed under "Pokémon Character Designer". This is a résumé shared by Reiko Tanoue and Mana Ibe, who both illustrated a single card from the Arceus expansion and are listed under the same roles in both sets of credits.

name: match
bio: match is a Japanese digital illustrator who began providing artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game in 2009, with their first illustrations debuting in the HeartGold & SoulSilver expansion. Like similar digital artists, match applies many strokes utilizing a graphics tablet in image editing software to create their images. match uses pattern brushes in select areas to achieve the desired texture in some illustrations, and often uses a subtle color palette combined with emphasis on light and shadow to help define the main subject, frequently accompanied by a prominent outline. In some cases, this technique gives an illusion of a 3D rendered model. In addition to providing artwork for the Pokémon TCG, match also began providing art for the Dimension-Zero TCG in 2010.

name: K. Hoshiba
bio: Kei Hoshiba (Japanese: 保志場慶) is a 3D graphic designer primarily involved with the development of character models in several early Pokémon titles and more recently, environment design on the latest titles. He has also produced artwork for a number of cards in the Pokémon Trading Card Game, though is often credited as K. Hoshiba.[1]

name: Mizue
bio: Mizue (Japanese: 瑞絵) is a freelance illustrator and manga artist who has contributed artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Her first cards were Snubbull and Granbull from the Call of Legends expansion. Many of her subjects are portrayed in dynamic poses, and colored using soft palettes and gradients with a definitive outline. The backgrounds of her artwork are more adventurous, particularly those that feature foliage, with individual leaves and plants incorporated into various gradient layers complete with a combination of halftone dots and horizontal lines. The majority of her subjects often include a white glow to help them stand out from the background. Bubbles and sparkles using lens flare also feature in many of her illustrations. While she engages in producing personal drawings and comic strips, the majority of her professional work involves providing art for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Saya Tsuruta
bio: Saya Tsuruta (Japanese: 鶴田沙綾 / つるたさや Tsuruta Saya) is a designer and illustrator for the Pokémon games and the Pokémon Trading Card Game. After graduating from Tama Art University,[2] her first game credits were on Pokémon Diamond and Pearl, though her contributions are unknown as she's only listed under Special Thanks. By the release of Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver, Tsuruta had become a graphic designer, creating all of the location previews in the game, stating that it took a lot of hard work.[3] Her contributions to the TCG began with Lotad from the Secret Wonders expansion.
trivia:
Almost every single Pokémon TCG artwork done by Saya Tsuruta contains a hidden image of a Poké Ball in the background. The only exceptions are as follows:
Tsuruta's Shiny Vault cards from Hidden Fates, Shining Fates, and Paldean Fates (which use a plain white background with generic Shiny sparkle effects).
The Yokohama's Pikachu cards (which use a generic striped background).
The SWSH Black Star Promos Pikachu V-UNION (a collaboration between Tsuruta and 24 other artists; the cards use a generic gradient background).
Paldean Wooper from Paldea Evolved (according to Tsuruta in an apology, the Poké Ball in this card had "rolled off the frame").[11]
Tsuruta's Shiny Vault cards from Hidden Fates, Shining Fates, and Paldean Fates (which use a plain white background with generic Shiny sparkle effects).
The Yokohama's Pikachu cards (which use a generic striped background).
The SWSH Black Star Promos Pikachu V-UNION (a collaboration between Tsuruta and 24 other artists; the cards use a generic gradient background).
Paldean Wooper from Paldea Evolved (according to Tsuruta in an apology, the Poké Ball in this card had "rolled off the frame").[11]
Tsuruta's favorite Pokémon is Vulpix.[12]

name: kodama
bio: kodama (Japanese: 小玉) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Gastly from the Generations expansion.

name: You Iribi
bio: You Iribi (Japanese: 伊里日(いりび)葉(よう)) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, who has been illustrating since Fates Collide starting with Serperior.

name: Hideki Ishikawa
bio: Hideki Ishikawa (Japanese: 石川(いしかわ)ヒデキ Ishikawa Hideki) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. He was also involved in character illustrations for Pokémon Duel. His first card was Magmar from the Generations expansion. Outside of Pokémon, Ishikawa was the character designer and illustrator for games in the Disgaea and Mega Man series, as well as other trading card games.

name: Tomokazu Komiya
bio: Tomokazu Komiya (Japanese: こみやトモカズ Komiya Tomokazu; born 1973) is an illustrator who has provided art for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, as well as several Pokémon Tales books. His illustration style is well known within the Pokémon community particularly due to his deformed and loosely colored images. This is intentional, as Komiya is a practitioner of Primitivism, an art movement that takes inspiration from themes or stylistic elements of prehistory, tribal cultures, or children's art. For the 2023 "Pokémon x Van Gogh" art collaboration, Komiya contributed illustrations of Sunflora and Smeargle, inspired by Vincent van Gogh's Sunflowers and Self-Portrait as a Painter, respectively.

name: Shigenori Negishi
bio: Shigenori Negishi (Japanese: ネギシシゲノリ) is an illustrator based in Chigasaki City,[1] who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Hitmontop from the Call of Legends expansion.

name: Kent Kanetsuna
bio: Kent Kanetsuna (Japanese: 金綱賢人 Kanetsuna Kento) is an illustrator who contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game in Generation IV and V. The first card they illustrated was Lucario from the Diamond & Pearl Trainer Kit. Their final illustration was featured in the Legendary Treasures expansion. However, Donphan from the HeartGold & SoulSilver expansion was reprinted in the Celebrations Classic Collection during the Sword & Shield Series. In total, Kanetsuna illustrated 71 cards (excluding reprints). A full list of cards they illustrated can be found here.

name: chibi
bio: chibi is an illustrator who has contributed artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Azelf, one of the XY Black Star Promos.

name: Hasuno
bio: Hasuno (Japanese: はすの; born February 15) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Golem from the Generations expansion.

name: Ryota Murayama
bio: Ryota Murayama (Japanese: 村山(むらやま)竜大(りょうた)), also known as ovopack, is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. He has been illustrating since Flashfire starting with Druddigon. He has also illustrated the booster packs for the Roaring Skies[citation needed] and Ancient Origins expansions.[citation needed]

name: Hiromichi Sugiyama
bio: Hiromichi Sugiyama is an artist who worked for Creatures, Inc. on various Pokémon media, including multiple spin-off Pokémon games, the Pokémon Trading Card Game, and the Pokémon Trading Figure Game.

name: HiRON
bio: Hirofumi Nakano (Japanese: 中野博文), born in Tokyo, is a 3D illustrator who has provided artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game on a few occasions, with his first appearing in the Dragons Exalted expansion. He is normally credited as "HiRON" (ハイロン) in his work. Nakano is a member of DigitalImage, a part-time digital design lecturer at the Niigata College of Art & Design, and a part-time illustration lecturer at the Tokyo Designer Gakuin College. His work primarily features on covers and in articles of computing and car magazines. Subjects are often exaggerated versions of their normal counterparts, with vehicles such as cars and aircraft created to make them appear more futuristic, and anthropomorphized animals with proportionally larger body parts. Among his interests, he often delves into the realms of science fiction and animation for his work, with images including various types of mecha or assorted creatures. Many of his images are illuminated with an intense light and textured with a highly reflective surface. Nakano regularly participates in producing exhibition work, and has also branched into producing some of his work into jewelry, as well as creating traditional Japanese illustrations for smart phone cases and music players. For a complete list of cards that HiRON has illustrated, go here.

name: Yukiko Baba
bio: Yukiko Baba (Japanese: 馬場(ばば)由起子(ゆきこ)) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Her first cards were Weepinbell and Tauros from the Expansion Sheet Series 3. Her first card for an English set was Kakuna from the Neo Discovery expansion.

name: Hideaki Hakozaki
bio: Hideaki Hakozaki (Japanese: 箱崎秀明 Hakozaki Hideaki), born September 29, 1977, Yokohama, is a painter, illustrator and 3D designer. He is a graduate of the University of Art and Design in Tokyo, having majored in oil painting, and has been living and working in the city since. In April 2001, he became a 3D designer employed at Hudson Soft. Determined not to stay within one area of expertise, he ventured into illustration. Going freelance in January 2007, he undertook commissions for various companies and developed his own unique painting style. He became an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game in 2009 with the debut of the HeartGold & SoulSilver expansion. In September 2011, he founded his own design studio called PLANETA.

name: BERUBURI
bio: BERUBURI was an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. BERUBURI has illustrated 4 cards, excluding reprints. For a list of cards illustrated by BERUBURI, go here.
trivia: All the Pokédex entries of the cards illustrated by BERUBURI comes from the Generation V games, either being from Pokémon Black and White or Pokémon Black 2 and White 2.

name: Shizurow
bio: Shizurow is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first illustrations were featured in the EX Crystal Guardians expansion.

name: ryoma uratsuka
bio: ryoma uratsuka (Japanese: うらつかりょうま Uratsuka Ryōma) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Drifloon from the Unified Minds expansion.

name: Megumi Mizutani
bio: Megumi Mizutani (Japanese: 水谷恵 Mizutani Megumi) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game and one of the Pokémon designers since Generation V, thus leading to other credits, such as conceptual character artist for Pokémon the Series: Black & White. She has also drawn several characters for Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire and Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!. She has provided illustrations for 105 different cards (excluding reprints), starting in the Black & White Series with Pansage.

name: KEIICHIRO ITO
bio: KEIICHIRO ITO (Japanese: イトウケイイチロウ Ito Keiichirō) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His first card was Magmortar from the Unified Minds expansion.

name: otumami
bio: otumami (Japanese: おつまみ) is a freelance artist that contributes to the Pokémon series, with her debut as an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, her first contribution being Clawitzer from the Forbidden Light expansion. In 2021, she had the opportunity to be the concept artist for Pokémon Evolutions, in addition to her first credited Pokémon game work as a promotional artist for Pokémon Masters EX. With the release of HZ018, she was brought on as the color scripter of the episode.[2] In 2023, she worked on a core series game for the very first time, as a promotional artist for Pokémon Scarlet and Violet's Darkrai event.

name: Ken Ikuji
bio: Ken Ikuji is an artist who worked for Tomcat System and later Creatures, Inc. as a designer and Pokémon modeler. He also provided illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Kimiya Masago
bio: Kimiya Masago  (Japanese: 正子公也), born 1960, Okayama, is a freelance illustrator and emaki artist whose works primarily depict characters from Chinese and Japanese history, particularly those from Romance of the Three Kingdoms, The Water Margin (Suikoden), and various military leaders from the Sengoku period. Masago earned a bachelor's degree majoring in physics at Chuo University in 1983, and became a freelance artist in 1989. His first work, a manga series entitled Clown with Blue Nose, was first published in 1990. He has since gone on to produce many illustrations for numerous publications, even branching into the film industry in 2005, where he became a costume designer for the Chinese film The Promise. Masago provided illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game between 2000 and 2005, depicting a number of Pokémon in a similar fashion to his traditional work, focusing on tone, areas of extreme color, and atmospheric environments. For a list of all cards he has illustrated, go here.

name: nagimiso
bio: nagimiso (Japanese: 凪水そう) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first cards were Team Aqua's Kyogre-EX and Team Magma's Groudon-EX from the Double Crisis expansion. After a two-and-a-half-year period without any cards from this illustrator, they returned for the Burning Shadows expansion, and have illustrated a large number of cards since.

name: Taira Akitsu
bio: Taira Akitsu (Japanese: 秋津たいら Akitsu Taira) is an Osaka-based illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Vulpix from the Sword & Shield expansion.

name: Sanosuke Sakuma
bio: Sanosuke Sakuma (Japanese: 佐久間さのすけ Sakuma Sanosuke; born October 31, 1990)[2] is a freelance illustrator living in Kanagawa,[2] who began providing artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game in 2013, with her first illustrations featured on cards released in the Shiny Collection. During her career with the TCG, she began working as a character designer on Pokémon Sun and Moon and Pokémon Sword and Shield, where she created many of the games' various Trainer classes. She draws digitally, opting to use Adobe Photoshop as her application of choice.[2] Sakuma states that she began drawing from an early age with a particular interest in anime and manga, and was head of a manga club while at high school and college. She specializes in producing artwork with cute characters and invoking a warm atmosphere, utilizing a specific color palette and soft drawing style. She also experiments with different styles, including anime, impasto, and watercolor, and likes to convey a sense of motion in images that require it.
trivia: Sakuma's favorite Pokémon are Keldeo and Quaquaval.[10]

name: Tomoko Wakai
bio: Tomoko Wakai is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. The only expansion that this person illustrated cards for was the EX Deoxys expansion.

name: Takumi Akabane
bio: Takumi Akabane is a former research and development director at Creatures, Inc., having been a part of the company since at least 1994, when he was listed as a chief debugger on the game EarthBound, before resigning in 2008. He is credited with creating the Pokémon Trading Card Game alongside Tsunekazu Ishihara and Kouichi Ooyama, and acted as its creative director from 2001 to 2008, after which he was succeeded in that role by Atsushi Nagashima. Akabane has a cameo appearance as Club Master Akabane (Ken in the English version of the game).

name: Masako Yamashita
bio: Masako Yamashita (Japanese: 山下雅子) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first cards were Kingler, Gastly, Hypno, and Kangaskhan from the Japanese Expansion Sheet Series 3. Their first English cards released in the Neo Revelation expansion.

name: Zu-Ka
bio: Zu-Ka is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: aky CG Works
bio: aky CG Works is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Thus far, aky CG Works has illustrated 86 cards (excluding reprints), the first of which was Kangaskhan-GX, one of the SM Black Star Promos. A full list of cards illustrated by aky CG Works can be found here.

0313 (pronounced Zero San Ichi San in Japanese[1]), is a Kyushu-based freelance illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game.[1] Their first card was Lampent from the Guardians Rising expansion. 0313 creates their illustrations using Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator.[1]
trivia: 0313's nickname is directly based on their birthday, March 13.

name: Hitoshi Ariga
bio: Hitoshi Ariga (Japanese: 有賀 ヒトシ Ariga Hitoshi; born August 23, 1972) is a professional artist who primarily illustrates manga and picture books, and has assumed the position of graphic designer for several Japanese titles in the game industry. He first began providing illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game in 2011, though has been a fan of the franchise for many years. His main passion, however, lies with the Mega Man franchise, known as Rockman in Japan, where he has illustrated numerous manga and artwork for affiliated products since the mid-90s. He likes to engage the community when he has the opportunity, appearing at exhibitions, and maintaining an online presence across several sites. Ken Sugimori recognized Ariga's design work and invited him to work on Pokémon X and Y.[2] When designing Amaura and Aurorus, Ariga considered that a sauropod would pair well with Tyrunt and Tyrantrum, suggesting that the latter may have been considered first. Previous Pokémon such as Lapras, Meganium, and Deino already existed with a similar body shape, so Ariga chose to base the new family off the Amargasaurus, with the large fins on its neck.[3] In creating the artwork for the villainous organization 3DS themes, Ariga pointed out the special attention given to how it looped seamlessly as the user navigated the 3DS menu.[4] In the same thread, he also revealed that there were plans to create a 3DS theme for Team Flare, but they fell through as a result of the series moving from the 3DS to the Switch.[5] Ariga's first spot as the lead character designer on the series was with Pokémon UNITE, though his affinity for paleontology led him to create a new design for Pikachu for the real-life Pokémon Fossil Museum, where he was reached out to by the organizers of the museum themselves. Although he began officially working on the series in 2011 with the TCG, his Pokémon fan art on DeviantArt dates back to 2010. From as early as 2011, Ariga would upload online battles against other players to his YouTube channel, which was something that he continued with well after the release of Pokémon Sword and Shield.[6] Though they were uploaded to what was originally his main YouTube channel, Ariga has recently shifted focus to regularly live streaming art with his VTuber avatar.[7]
trivia:
Hitoshi Ariga's favorite Pokémon is Misdreavus, as can be seen in an archive of his Twitter bio.[80]
He also designed its assumed ancient relative, Flutter Mane.
He also designed its assumed ancient relative, Flutter Mane.
Ariga enjoyed the battle between Ash and Sawyer at the Lumiose Conference, so much so that he drew the latter with Aegislash when drawing fan-art of the Pokémon.[81]

name: Makoto Imai
bio: Makoto Imai is an illustrator of some Pokémon TCG cards.

name: miki kudo
bio: miki kudo (Japanese: くどうみき Kudō Miki) an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Butterfree from the Generations expansion.

name: DemizuPosuka
bio: DemizuPosuka (出水 ぽすか) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, who has been illustrating since Generations starting with Rapidash. She has also illustrated for Pokémon Masters EX.[1] Outside of Pokémon, she has illustrated for the manga series The Promised Neverland and several other trading card games.

name: hatachu
bio: hatachu (Japanese: ハタチュウ) is a 3D CG illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Charizard from the Boundaries Crossed expansion.

name: Hiroyuki Yamamoto
bio: Hiroyuki Yamamoto (Japanese: ヤマモトヒロユキ Yamamoto Hiroyuki) is a character designer and illustrator for the Pokémon franchise. He began working on the series with the Sun & Moon expansion of the Pokémon Trading Card Game, contributing 3D illustrations for the expansion's booster packs and Dragonite card. Yamamoto uses the series' official 3D models as a base, utilizing photobashing and other rendering techniques to make his art for the TCG.[2] Yamamoto is also the character designer and sole credited artist for Pokémon Café ReMix. Unlike his earlier TCG work, Yamamoto uses a distinctive 2D style for this game. Other video games they have designed for include Monkey King: Hero is Back[citation needed] and Dillon's Dead-Heat Breakers.[citation needed]

name: Saki Hayashiro
bio: Saki Hayashiro (Japanese: はやしろ咲 Hayashiro Saki) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Thus far, Saki Hayashiro has illustrated 23 cards, the first of which was Ninetales V from the Rebel Clash expansion. A full list of cards illustrated by Saki Hayashiro can be found here.

name: Uta
bio: Uta is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Ponyta from the Cosmic Eclipse expansion.

name: Hikaru Koike
bio: Hikaru Koike is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game and Pokémon Trading Figure Game. For a list of cards illustrated by Hikaru Koike, go here.

name: Kazuo Yazawa
bio: Kazuo Yazawa (Japanese: やざわ かずお Kazuo Yazawa) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game who previously worked at Creatures Inc. He is credited as a graphic designer and 3D modeler for several Pokémon games, including the Pokémon Stadium series and Pokémon Ranger, among other titles. Outside of the Pokémon franchise, Yazawa has worked at HAL Laboratory, Inc. as a sub-game designer, among other credits, on various Kirby series games.

name: Asako Ito
bio: Asako Ito is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Her first card was Poliwag from the Sun & Moon expansion. She is unique among TCG artists as, rather than drawing or making a 3D render, she crochets amigurumi of the subject.

name: Mikiko Takeda
bio: Mikiko Takeda is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. They have only illustrated 2 cards in the TCG. They have also worked on three side games, particularly in the graphics and animation department. A full list of cards illustrated by Mikiko Takeda can be found here.

name: Toyste Beach
bio: Toyste Beach (Japanese: トイストビーチ Toyste Beach) is a game and video development studio that has contributed to illustrations of cards for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, starting with Mewtwo-EX in Next Destinies. They have illustrated a small number of Pokémon cards, but are mostly known for their Trainer cards. Their artists have been known to illustrate both 3D CG and 2D on drawing programs.

name: Tomoaki Imakuni
bio: Tomoaki Imakuni (Japanese: 今国智章 Imakuni Tomoaki), usually referred to as Imakuni? (イマクニ？ Imakuni?), is a staff member at Creatures, Inc. involved in various aspects of the TCG, including illustrations and other appearances on several cards.[1] Imakuni is known as an eccentric musician who performed some of the music for Pokémon the Series. Imakuni? played a small part in the designing of Pokémon Ranger and its sequel, Shadows of Almia. He is in the band Suzukisan. He is also credited as the author of the Pokémon Tales picture book "Come Out, Squirtle!". Additionally, Imakuni? starred in his own card game titled Bakaboom : Composition Game So Hard Your Brain Will Spill Out.[2]
trivia: Imakuni's favorite Pokémon is Binacle.[3]
Imakuni is a member of Team Instinct in Pokémon GO.[4]
Imakuni keeps his black bodysuit in a drawer by his desk. He wears the bodysuit when he sings karaoke.[5]

Imakuni appears nostalgic for the game "Monster Tactics", which, according to the credits, was co-produced by Tsunekazu Ishihara with Takehiro Izushi for his and Nintendo's company Spiral, supported by Marigul Management and linked with Creatures, Inc..[6]

name: Takashi Yamaguchi
bio: Takashi Yamaguchi is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. He started illustrating cards from the HeartGold & SoulSilver expansion, specifically Meganium. So far, he has illustrated 18 cards for the Trading Card Game. For a list of cards he illustrated, go here.

name: T. Honda
bio: T. Honda is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Misa Tsutsui
bio: Misa Tsutsui (Japanese: 筒井(つつい)海砂(みさ); born 1970) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Tapu Lele, one of the SM-P Promotional cards.

name: PLANETA
bio: PLANETA (Japanese: プラネッタ) is a Japanese design studio founded by illustrator Hideaki Hakozaki in September 2011 that specializes in 3D computer generated imagery for consumer games and graphical production, such as illustrations. Hakozaki established the studio with the drive to employ a new generation of artists to create and engineer new methods of delivering digital content that people can play with. It is currently based in Higashi-nihombashi, Chūō, Tokyo and, as of April 2023, has 18 employees. Much of the studio's portfolio centers on package artwork for Gundam model kits and producing 3D models for numerous games across several platforms. Within the Pokémon franchise, PLANETA has contributed towards the development of titles in the Pokémon Mystery Dungeon series, produced key visuals for Pokémon GO, and produced artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game and for Pokémon Trading Card Game Pocket. PLANETA as a studio began illustrating cards from the Flashfire expansion. The studio is credited as PLANETA CG Works in TCG Pocket.[1] Individual artists began to be credited separately from the Forbidden Light expansion. These include: The studio also began producing booster pack art from the Japanese Plasma Gale expansion and has continued to do so throughout subsequent TCG Eras, going on to produce art for booster packs and Theme Decks released outside Asia beginning with the BREAKthrough expansion. PLANETA also produced key visuals for Japanese TCG events and other boxed products. With the official release of the TCG in Thailand and Indonesia, the studio was also commissioned to provide booster pack art for the first four localized sets.

name: Sachiko Adachi
bio: Sachiko Adachi is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. It is unknown how she actually illustrates her cards, as they are clearly not traditionally drawn; most fans believe they are either computer-generated images, like much of Pokémon art today, decoupages, or clay models, as of those by Yuka Morii. Her first illustrations were featured in the EX Team Rocket Returns expansion. For a list of cards illustrated by Sachiko Adachi, go here.

name: Kenkichi Toyama
bio: Kenkichi Toyama (Japanese: 外山健吉) is an artist who worked on the core series Pokémon games, having done graphic design as well as Pokémon designs. He has also done illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Ryuta Fuse
bio: Ryuta Fuse (Japanese: 布施(ふせ)龍太(りゅうた)) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was N's Resolve from the Cosmic Eclipse expansion.

name: Anesaki Dynamic
bio: Anesaki Dynamic (Japanese: 姉崎ダイナミック Anesaki Dynamic) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, who has been illustrating since Steam Siege starting with Persian. Anesaki Dynamic also illustrated the English package artwork for Brilliant Stars, Astral Radiance, Lost Origin, and Silver Tempest.[1]

name: Hiroki Fuchino
bio: Hiroki Fuchino (Japanese: 渕野大樹)  is an artist who has worked on multiple core series Pokémon games designing Pokémon and map graphics. He is also an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: "Big Mama" Tagawa
bio: Yoshiyuki Tagawa (Japanese: 田川喜之 Tagawa Yoshiyuki) is an graphic designer who worked at Creatures, Inc. They worked on 3D models for Pokémon and provided illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Tagawa has illustrated 46 cards (excluding reprints), credited as "Big Mama" Tagawa on cards they have illustrated.[1] All of their illustrations for the TCG are computer-generated graphics for Trainer Cards, with the only exception being the Neo Revelation Magneton. A full list of cards illustrated by "Big Mama" Tagawa can be found here.

name: PLANETA Otani
bio: Yuta Otani is an illustrator who has worked at PLANETA since 2012.[1] They have contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game, credited as PLANETA Otani on cards they have illustrated. A list of cards illustrated by them can be found here.

name: HYOGONOSUKE
bio: HYOGONOSUKE (ヒョーゴノスケ) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, who has been illustrating since Team Up starting with Jirachi. He has also done illustrations for Pokémon Quest.[2] Outside of Pokémon, HYOGONOSUKE has done illustrations for Love Live![2] and Doraemon[2], as well as created picture books and manga.

name: Hasegawa Saki
bio: Hasegawa Saki (Japanese: 長谷川早紀 Hasegawa Saki) is an animator and artist who contributed illustrations to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. A full list of cards illustrated by Hasegawa Saki can be found here.

name: Kazuaki Aihara
bio: Kazuaki Aihara was an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. The only set they illustrated cards for was Legends Awakened. For a list of cards illustrated by Kazuaki Aihara, go here.

name: Hiroaki Ito
bio: Hiroaki Ito is an graphic designer who has worked for Creatures, Inc. as a Pokémon modeler. Additionally, he has provided illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: James Turner
bio: James Turner, born 1978[1] is a British graphic designer who worked at Game Freak. In 2010, he became the first Westerner to officially design Pokémon. Turner designed Pokémon for Pokémon Black and White, Pokémon X and Y, Pokémon Sun and Moon, Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon, and Pokémon Sword and Shield; he was also the Art Director for the latter. Additionally, he directed the 2012 Nintendo 3DS eShop title HarmoKnight and the 2015 video game published by Sega, Tembo the Badass Elephant. Before joining Game Freak, James Turner worked for eight years at Genius Sonority, and was credited under the name Jamie Turner (Japanese: ジェイミー・ターナー). The first game he worked on at this company was Pokémon Colosseum, for which Turner was responsible for the game's battle effects, battle camera, and cutscenes.[2] For Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness, Turner finalized Shadow Lugia based on various initial sketches of the design drawn by Hiromoto-SIN-ichi, which began after the conceptualization of the core game.[3] Turner designed all the characters for Pokémon Battle Revolution and oversaw the designs of the different outfits.[4] He would then leave Genius Sonority to apply for another job, landing a position at GAME FREAK before the release of Pokémon Black and White.[3] During his interview, Turner claimed that he was required to design a Pokémon on the spot as part of the interview process. Although the moment was too fleeting to come up with a fully-fledged Pokémon with a backstory, Turner has mentioned that this design was originally a ghostly tree, which would later go on to spark the idea for the Phantump family in Pokémon X and Y.[3] On June 9, 2022, Turner announced that he had left Game Freak to form his own game studio, All Possible Futures.[5][6][7] This was a change that he had decided upon during the pre-production phase of Pokémon Scarlet and Violet, shortly following the end of Sword and Shield's development.[3]
trivia: While Turner has several Pokémon among his favorites,[51] as of April 29, 2018, Salandit is his favorite Pokémon.[52]

name: Christopher Rush
bio: Mewtwo (Japanese: ミュウツー Mewtwo) is a Psychic-type Basic Pokémon card. It was first released as one of the Wizards Black Star Promos.
trivia: The artwork change between the English and Japanese prints may have arisen due to the similarity of the Japanese artwork of this card to that of the first promo Mewtwo, as both are modified from Sugimori's Generation I stock art.

As the Japanese version of this card was originally distributed as part of an Expansion Sheet, it, along with Pikachu and Mew, are often regarded as unofficial additions to the Vending Machine cards collection, dubbed "Series 00".
In the manga adaptation of the second movie, this card is owned by Lawrence III.

name: Masahiko Ishii
bio: Masahiko Ishii is an artist who provided illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Noriko Hotta
bio: Noriko Hotta is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. She started illustrating cards starting from the HeartGold & SoulSilver Collection. She has now illustrated 22 cards for the TCG. For a list of cards she illustrated, look here.

name: Milky Isobe
bio: Milky Isobe (Japanese: ミルキィ・イソベ) is a former art director at Creatures, Inc. who worked on the Pokémon Trading Card Game from the beginning until the end of the Black & White Series.[1] Isobe has also provided illustrations for the TCG. Known for creating covers for magazines published by the now defunct Peyotl Kobo such as Yaso, Milky Isobe is responsible for starting Studio Parabolica and publishing the art magazine, YASO 2-. She has been working with computer graphics since the 1980s.

name: Jungo Suzuki
bio: Jungo Suzuki is an artist who worked for Creatures, Inc. as a Pokémon modeler. He also provided illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Benimaru Itoh
bio: Ashura Benimaru Itoh (Japanese: 伊藤あしゅら紅丸[1] Itoh Ashura Benimaru) is a manga artist, designer and musician who has drawn artwork for various Nintendo franchises. At Creatures, Inc., he worked as 3D modelling director for the Pokémon Stadium series games. He also illustrated Pokémon Newspaper Strip comics and several Pokémon Trading Card Game card artworks. In his Creatures, Inc. roles, he was typically credited as Benimaru Itoh (Japanese: 伊藤紅丸); however, for his work on Pokémon Newspaper Strip comics, he was instead credited as Ashura Benimaru. He likes to go by the nickname "Ash" (アシュ). Itoh is usually seen wearing his quirky leopard print attire.

name: Daisuke Iwamoto
bio: Daisuke Iwamoto was an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Iwamoto has illustrated 2 cards, excluding reprints. For a list of cards illustrated by Iwamoto, go here.

name: Kazuma Koda
bio: Kazuma Koda (Japanese: 幸田和磨 Koda Kazuma), also known as Lownine (Japanese: 浪人 Rōnin), is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Thus far, Koda has illustrated 15 cards, the first of which was Will from the Japanese Tag All Stars subset. Besides contributing artwork for the Pokémon TCG, Kazuma Koda has also contributed artwork for Project VOLTAGE, creating designs for Hatsune Miku as a Dark-type Pokémon Trainer. A full list of cards illustrated by Kazuma Koda can be found here.

name: Kunihiko Yuyama
bio: Kunihiko Yuyama (湯山邦彦) (b. 1952) is an animation director who has been involved with many of the products of Pokémon animation. He is also an illustrator for the TCG. Yuyama is one of the founding members of OLM, the animation studio that produces Pokémon animation. He began his career in the 1970s as an in-between artist on the original Space Battleship Yamato (aka Star Blazers in North America) and subsequently became an episode and series director on series for Tatsunoko Productions, Ashi Productions (now Production Reed), and Kaname Productions. Other than Pokémon, his most noteworthy work is likely the original Magical Princess Minky Momo series, on which he worked with the original Pokémon animation head writer Takeshi Shudō.
trivia: His favorite Pokémon is Lapras.
In This Could be the Start of Something Big!, Ash is shown battling a Trainer resembling Yuyama, who uses a Lapras.

With the end of Ash's saga in animation, the official Pokémon page on Twitter revealed an art containing the beginning of Ash's journey and his last scene in The Rainbow and the Pokémon Master! signed by Yuyama himself.[1]
Kunihiko Yuyama's cameo in This Could be the Start of Something Big!
Ash's farewell from animation autographed by Kunihiko Yuyama.

name: Mana Ibe
bio: Mana Ibe (Japanese: 井部真那, born November 27, 1985 in Tokyo) is a graphic designer who has worked for the Pokémon Trading Card Game and video game series. Ibe's first known involvement with the Pokémon franchise was in the staff of Pokémon Platinum under "Special Thanks", although it is currently unknown exactly what role she played in the development of that game. She later illustrated a card in the Arceus expansion: Manectric. In the staff of Pokémon Black and White, she is listed under "Pokémon Designer". This is a résumé shared by Keiko Moritsugu and Reiko Tanoue, who both illustrated a single card from the Arceus expansion and are listed under the same roles in both sets of credits. Ibe appears to have acquired a bigger role in Pokémon games since Pokémon Black and White. In a interview with Junichi Masuda, it was revealed that she designed Victini.[2] Along with Victini, she designed about 10 other Pokémon for Pokémon Black and White.[3] As of 2022, Ibe was appointed the art director of Pokémon Scarlet and Violet, her most senior role on the series thus far.
trivia: Ibe's favorite Pokémon is Herdier.[4][7]

name: so-taro
bio: so-taro (Japanese: 創-taro) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Thus far, so-taro has illustrated 19 cards, the first of which was Glalie from the Guardians Rising expansion. A full list of cards illustrated by so-taro can be found here.

name: Megumi Higuchi
bio: Megumi Higuchi is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Thus far, Higuchi has illustrated 18 cards (excluding reprints), the first of which was Ninetales from the Sword & Shield expansion. A full list of cards illustrated by Megumi Higuchi can be found here.

name: AKIRA EGAWA
bio: AKIRA EGAWA (Japanese: 江川(えがわ)あきら Egawa Akira) is a freelance illustrator who has worked on the Pokémon series. She began illustrating cards in 2019 for the Pokémon Trading Card Game with Riolu, included in the Unified Minds expansion. She has also illustrated for Pokémon Masters EX, providing artwork for the Dreams of the Void event. In addition to being an illustrator for cards themselves, EGAWA also illustrated booster pack artwork for the international releases of the Battle Styles, Chilling Reign, Evolving Skies, and Fusion Strike expansions. She was among the panel of judges for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Illustration Contest 2022. EGAWA's art style focuses on giving the subject detailed textures, with the goal of making them look "cool". She has previous experience with 3D modelling, but she currently primarily creates illustrations by painting in Photoshop. Credits outside Pokémon include other mobile and card games such as Fate/Grand Order, Fire Emblem Heroes and Cipher, and the One Piece Card Game.[1] EGAWA has been playing the Pokémon games since Generation II.[2]

name: Yoshinobu Saito
bio: Yoshinobu Saito is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first cards were Pikachu Libre and Suicune from the XY Trainer Kit: Pikachu Libre & Suicune deck kit.

name: Mt. TBT
bio: Mt. TBT is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Mt. TBT has illustrated 2 cards, excluding reprints. For a list of cards illustrated by Mt. TBT, go here. All cards illustrated by Mt. TBT are part of the EX Team Magma vs Team Aqua set.

name: Nobuyuki Fujimoto
bio: Nobuyuki Fujimoto (Japanese: 藤本 信行) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. He started illustrating cards for the Advent of Arceus Gym Challenge promotional card release, beginning his work with Porygon-Z G. So far, he has illustrated 2 cards for the Trading Card Game, and is expected to do more. For a list of cards he illustrated, go here.

name: Reiko Tanoue
bio: Reiko Tanoue (Japanese: 田上怜子) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. She has illustrated only two cards for the Trading Card Game: Sceptile, from the Arceus expansion, and Panpour from the Next Destinies expansion. She was also listed in the staff of Pokémon Platinum under "Special thanks" though it is currently unknown exactly what role she played in the development of that game. The staff of Pokémon Black and White lists her under "Pokémon designer". A résumé shared by Keiko Moritsugu and Mana Ibe, who both illustrated a single card from the Arceus expansion and are listed under the same roles in both sets of credits.
trivia: Tanoue's favorite Pokémon is Munna.[2]

name: PLANETA Tsuji
bio: PLANETA Tsuji is an illustrator at PLANETA who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Porygon-Z-GX, one of the SM Black Star Promos.

name: Emi Ando
bio: Emi Ando (Japanese: 安藤絵美) is an illustrator and a Pokémon designer for the Pokémon games. She has also been illustrating for the Pokémon Trading Card Game since Flashfire starting with Pokémon Fan Club.

name: M. Akiyama
bio: M. Akiyama was an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Akiyama has illustrated 3 cards. For a list of cards illustrated by M. Akiyama, go here.

name: Hiroki Asanuma
bio: Hiroki Asanuma (Japanese: 浅沼(あさぬま)寛樹(ひろき) Asanuma Hiroki) is a 3D CG illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. He also worked as a graphic designer for Pokémon Duel. His first card was Scizor from the Boundaries Crossed expansion.

name: Keita Komatsuya
bio: Keita Komatsuya is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Thus far, Komatsuya has only illustrated 1 card, being the Starmie from the Neo Revelation expansion. A full list of cards illustrated by Keita Komatsuya can be found here.

name: Gakuji Nomoto
