bio: Gakuji Nomoto is a photographer for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. So far, he has done 1 card, a promotional card of Pikachu. He is also a producer of various Pokémon Media. A list of cards taken by Gakuji Nomoto can be found here.

name: Yuri Umemura
bio: Yuri Umemura is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Yusuke Ohmura
bio: Yusuke Ohmura (Japanese: 大村祐介 Ōmura Yūsuke, born July 6, 1981) is an illustrator of the artwork for Pokémon games since Pokémon Diamond and Pearl. He has drawn several characters for the core series games starting with Pokémon Black and White, such as Gym Leaders and the Elite Four of Unova. Ohmura created the designs for Piplup, Oshawott, and the version mascots of Pokémon X and Y, Xerneas and Yveltal. Initial design for the two Legendary Pokémon was started by Ken Sugimori, but after he encountered 'artist's block', he gave the work to Ohmura, who furthered the designs. Sugimori later returned to finish them.[1] In Pokémon Sun and Moon, he became the lead of Pokémon designer, switching his role with Sugimori. In 2016, Ohmura left Game Freak and became a freelance illustrator.[2] He is also an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, starting with the Mysterious Treasures expansion. For a complete list of cards that Ohmura illustrated, go here.
trivia: Ohmura's favorite Pokémon is Reuniclus.[50]

name: Atsuko Ujiie
bio: Atsuko Ujiie (Japanese: 氏家淳子) is an executive director at Creatures, Inc. and the executive art director of the Pokémon CG Studio. She has worked on the Pokémon modeling staff throughout the series in both lead and support roles. She also contributed graphics to Pokémon Ranger, and was one of the CG directors for the ending animation of Pokémon the Movie 2000 - The Power of One. Ujiie is also an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Takao Unno
bio: Takao Unno (Japanese: 海野隆雄) is a graphic designer for Pokémon games since Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire. He was the art director for Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver, who was responsible for the design of new female protagonist Lyra.[1] He was appointed by Junichi Masuda as the director for Pokémon Black 2 and White 2. He is also an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game since the EX Deoxys expansion. His last illustration in many years was Team Rocket's Trickery from the Undaunted expansion. For a complete list of cards that Unno illustrated, see here.

name: GAME FREAK inc.
bio: Game Freak, Inc. (Japanese: 株式会社ゲームフリーク Kabushiki gaisha Game Freak), officially stylized as GAME FREAK inc. or less commonly as GAMEFREAK inc., is a Japanese game development company founded on April 26, 1989 by Satoshi Tajiri, Ken Sugimori, and Junichi Masuda. Game Freak is responsible for the development of the core series Pokémon games, as well as the free-to-play spin-off game Pokémon Quest, and shares ownership of The Pokémon Company with Creatures, Inc. and Nintendo. The company has 207 employees as of March 2024,[1] while Satoshi Tajiri serves as its representative director. Its headquarters were initially located on the Kashiwa 3rd building in Shimokitazawa.[2][3] It moved to Carrot Tower on November 19, 2007[4] and to Kanda Square in Nishikichō between May and July 2020.[5][6] Game Freak launched its website on January 29, 1997.[7] Between October 1999 and November 1999, the head office address and phone numbers were removed.[8][9] The address would then be readded during summer 2007.[10][11] On September 17, 2020, it was reported on Weibo that Game Freak trademarked its Chinese name as 遊戲狂想家 Game Maniac after changing it from 遊戲富利克 Game Freak.[12][13] In Korean, the company is called 게임프리크 Game Freak. Game Freak acquired and absorbed the mobile development company Koa Games in October 2015.[14]

name: NC Empire
bio: NC Empire (Japanese: NC帝國) is an illustration group that has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game, the first of which was Luxio from the Shining Fates expansion, first released as one of the S-P Promotional cards.

name: Satoshi Ohta
bio: Satoshi Ohta is an artist who worked for Game Freak. He designed Pokémon in Generation II through Generation IV in addition to his graphic design work. Ohta also provided illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Tika Matsuno
bio: Tika Matsuno (Japanese: 松野(まつの)千歌(ちか) Matsuno Chika) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, making her debut in the Darkness Ablaze expansion. She would later go on to be a Holowear designer for Pokémon UNITE. Matsuno has also drawn manga and Illustrations for the Pokémon Cafe in Tokyo.[citation needed]

name: Hideki Kazama
bio: Hideki Kazama is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Souichirou Gunjima
bio: Souichirou Gunjima (Japanese: 軍島曹一郎 Gunjima Sōichirō) is a freelance illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Before illustrating for the TCG in an official capacity, Gunjima was a participant in the Pokémon Card Game Illustration Grand Prix, where he submitted an illustration of Metagross. The first official card he illustrated was Indeedee from the Shining Fates expansion. Gunjima has also illustrated TCG merchandise such as the Fire Stacking Tin.
trivia: Souichirou Gunjima's favorite Pokémon is Kabutops. On October 20, 2021, Gunjima tweeted that one of his dreams is to draw an official illustration of Kabutops.[3] In 2023, the 151 special set of the Pokémon Trading Card Game was released, featuring a Kabutops card illustrated by Gunjima.[4]

name: sadaji
bio: sadaji is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Thus far, sadaji has illustrated 28 cards (excluding reprints), the first of which were featured in the Unbroken Bonds expansion. sadaji has illustrated a small number of Pokémon-GX and Pokémon V, but is mainly known for their Item cards, specifically their gold etched Secret cards. A full list of cards illustrated by sadaji can be found here.

name: kanahei
bio: kanahei (Japanese: カナヘイ) is an illustrator who has worked for the TCG. She also worked as an artist for Pokémon Smile.

name: Yosuke Da Silva
bio: Yosuke Da Silva is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. The only expansion that this illustrator illustrated cards for was EX Team Magma vs Team Aqua.

name: Emi Yoshida
bio: Emi Yoshida (Japanese: 吉田絵美) is an artist who worked on the core Generation IV Pokémon games as a graphic designer and Pokémon designer. She also worked as an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Craig Turvey
bio: Illustration contests are contests in which entrants are invited to create artwork of requested Pokémon in an effort to have it featured on a card in the Pokémon Trading Card Game. The majority of these contests have only been open to residents of Japan, with many earlier competitions held in Shogakukan publications, such as CoroCoro Comic. Wizards of the Coast and The Pokémon Company International have also held contests in North America and many other countries worldwide during their tenure. The following is a list of contests held in conjunction with the TCG.

name: take
bio: take (Japanese: 竹(たけ)) is a professional artist and character designer for the Pokémon series. She has also contributed several illustrations to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. She draws digitally, opting to use Adobe Photoshop as her application of choice.[1]

name: Maiko Fujiwara
bio: Maiko Fujiwara is a graphic designer for the Pokémon games since Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver. She is also an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, though has only illustrated two cards: Musharna from the Next Destinies expansion and Pokémon Center Lady regular print from the Flashfire expansion.

name: Studio Bora Inc.
bio: Studio Bora Inc. (Japanese: スタジオ ボーラ株式会社) is a company that has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Thus far, Studio Bora Inc. has illustrated 67 cards, the first of which was Skuntank from the Ultra Prism expansion.

name: Asuka Iwashita
bio: Asuka Iwashita (Japanese: 岩下明日香) is a conceptual character artist for Pokémon the Series, specifically the sixth, seventh, and twelfth Pokémon movies. In addition to these three movies, she worked on the special episode The Mastermind of Mirage Pokémon. In addition to working on Pokémon the Series, Iwashita worked as a graphic designer for multiple Pokémon games from Pokémon Gold and Silver through Pokémon Emerald. In addition to being a designer for the games' graphics, she is also credited for designing Pokémon in Generation III. As an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, Asuka Iwashita illustrated 5 cards, beginning in 2001. Her first illustrations were featured in Pokémon VS, in which she illustrated all of Sabrina's featured Pokémon. In 2004, three years after illustrating these cards, she was credited as an illustrator for the last time on Makuhita.

name: Hizuki Misono
bio: Hizuki Misono (Japanese: 御園日月 Misono Hizuki) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. She is also a staff member of the Pokémon Mystery Dungeon series games and one of its animated specials. She is a staff member to other games, including Pokémon Colosseum.

name: Aimi Tomita
bio: Aimi Tomita is an artist who worked as a graphic designer and Pokémon designer for the Generation III core series games. She was also a concept artist for the character designs for the movies Destiny Deoxys, Jirachi Wish Maker and Arceus and the Jewel of Life, as well as the special The Mastermind of Mirage Pokémon. Additionally, she made illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Aimi has illustrated 3 cards (excluding reprints). A full list of cards illustrated by Aimi can be found here.

name: Narumi Sato
bio: Narumi Sato (Japanese: さとうなるみ Satō Narumi) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. She was the runner-up in the Pokémon Card Game Illustration Grand Prix, where she submitted artwork of Eevee. Since then, Sato has been a regular illustrator of official cards, the first of which was Manaphy from the Shining Fates expansion. Sato paints her illustrations for the TCG traditionally using transparent watercolor. Her favorite Pokémon is Archeops.[1]

name: Kouji Tajima
bio: Kouji Tajima is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. So far, he has illustrated two cards from Plasma Storm, Lunatone and Solrock. For a list of cards illustrated by Kouji Tajima, go here.

name: The Pokémon Company Art Team
bio: The Pokémon Company (株式会社ポケモン Kabushiki gaisha Pokémon) is a company responsible for the licensing and marketing of the Pokémon franchise. Founded on April 23, 1998 with the name The Pokémon Center Company (ポケモンセンター株式会社 Pokémon Center kabushiki gaisha) as a joint venture by Nintendo, Game Freak, and Creatures, it was created to manage the Pokémon Center stores in Japan.[1] It has since expanded to be responsible for the game software, card games, license management, TV animation and films, and other ancillary businesses in Japan and Asia.[2] Its wholly owned subsidiaries, Pokémon Korea, Inc. and The Pokémon Company International, manage these responsibilities in South Korea and areas outside Asia, respectively.[3][4] In March 2024, The Pokémon Company and ILCA established The Pokémon Works as a joint venture. As of September 2019, The Pokémon Company had sold over 346 million units of their video games and shipped over 28.8 billion trading cards.[5] Tsunekazu Ishihara is the President and CEO of the company.

name: Tomohiro Kitakaze
bio: Tomohiro Kitakaze (Japanese: 北風友裕, born April 8th, 1983 in Kobe) is a freelance illustrator. He is an Osaka University of Arts graduate and previously worked at Monolith Soft as a 2D designer, providing concept art for characters, monsters, and machinery. He later worked for Game Freak, again as a 2D designer, providing concept art and designs for Pokémon characters, though it is unknown how many Pokémon he has designed. In addition, he also provided artwork for one card from the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Kitakaze's subjects are initially drawn traditionally, and then enhanced digitally afterwards. His cartoon strips and characters are created in anime style, though his more detailed illustration work draws inspiration from mythical creatures and the occult, sometimes incorporating mechanical motifs. He claims that his design for Mega Mewtwo Y was influenced by his adoration for Mewtwo Strikes Back as a child.[1]

name: Hideyuki Nakajima
bio: Hideyuki Nakajima is an artist who provided illustrations for the Generation III Pokémon games and has illustrated 1 card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. They have also been credited for typesetting and layout on the TCG.[1]

name: Etsuya Hattori
bio: Etsuya Hattori (Japanese: 服部悦也) was an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His first illustration was Sunkern, a card released in the Neo Destiny expansion in March of 2001. He is also credited as the illustrator for all of Lt. Surge's Pokémon in the Pokémon VS expansion. Not only had Hattori worked for the Trading Card Game, but he had worked in Graphic Support for the Pokémon Channel spin-off game. In total, he illustrated 3 cards for the trading card game. For the complete list of cards he illustrated, go here.

name: Yuichi Sawayama
bio: Yuichi Sawayama is an artist who worked for Creatures, Inc. as a Pokémon modeler. He also provided illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

name: Shinji Higuchi
bio:
Shinji Higuchi (Japanese: 樋口真嗣), born September 22, 1965, Tokyo, is a writer, director, storyboard artist and a prominent special effects figure in Japanese film and television. As a teenager he was one of the four founding members of Gainax (originally established as Daicon Films), working on many anime and tokusatsu productions. He played an important part in the creation of the popular anime series Neon Genesis Evangelion, serving as writer, assistant director, and art director/storyboarder. His previous work on the anime Nadia: The Secret of Blue Water led the show's director and fellow Gainax member Hideaki Anno to name Evangelion's protagonist, Shinji Ikari after him as an inside joke.
Higuchi initially started his career in the mid 80s working within special effects on several kaiju films, and by the mid 90's had established himself as a master within the field with the release of the acclaimed Gamera trilogy of films. During this time, he continued to be a storyboarder for anime such as Gunbuster and Otaku no Video, his wife also providing the namesake for the former's heroine, Noriko Takaya. In addition to his special effects direction, Higuchi branched into CG animation for several tokusatsu films in the early 2000s, and has since directed a number of live-action films. Higuchi became involved within the Pokémon franchise during the production of Jirachi: Wish Maker as a storyboard artist in 2004. He was later commissioned to produce the artwork for the new Pokémon LEGEND cards that first appeared in the HeartGold & SoulSilver expansion of the Pokémon Trading Card Game, and went on to co-illustrate all subsequent Pokémon LEGEND cards released in the HeartGold & SoulSilver Series. He was also involved in the art direction of two cards from the Undaunted expansion in collaboration with 3D illustrator Kent Kanetsuna.

name: Noriko Takaya

She is the wife of special effects master and Gainax member Shinji Higuchi. She is also the namesake of the heroine of Gunbuster, one of Gainax's first anime series, whom Higuchi named after her. name: 2017 Pikachu Project
bio: Pokémon the Movie: I Choose You! (Japanese: 劇場版ポケットモンスター　キミにきめた！ Pocket Monsters the Movie: I Choose You!; officially known as Pokémon the Movie 20: I choose you! in Japan) is the twentieth Pokémon movie, and the first released during the broadcast of Pokémon the Series: Sun & Moon. It premiered with Japanese vocals and French subtitles at Japan Expo on July 6, 2017. It was released in Japan on July 15, 2017, and received a limited release in North American, South American, and European theaters starting on November 5, 2017, in Australia and New Zealand starting on November 11, 2017, in Singapore starting on November 23, 2017, and in Malaysia starting on December 7, 2017. It premiered on Disney XD on November 25, 2017 as part of a marathon including Mounting an Electrifying Charge! and Alola, Kanto!. It was first revealed in a teaser trailer that aired on Oha Suta in Japan on December 15, 2016. The full trailer was later released on March 2, 2017. A new trailer was released on April 8, 2017, officially revealing Marshadow to have a role in the film. In a departure from the previous movies, this movie is a loose reboot of Ash's original journey through the Kanto region, in celebration of the 20th anniversary of the Pokémon animated series. It is the first movie of a trilogy and is followed by The Power of Us, Secrets of the Jungle, and Distant Blue Sky!.[1]

name: 2019 Pikachu Project
bio: Pokémon: Mewtwo Strikes Back—Evolution (Japanese: ミュウツーの逆襲 EVOLUTION  Mewtwo's Counterattack Evolution, officially known as Mewtwo Strikes Back Evolution in Japan) is the twenty-second Pokémon movie overall, and the third released during the broadcast of Pokémon the Series: Sun & Moon. It is a CGI remake of the first movie, Mewtwo Strikes Back. It premiered with Japanese audio and English subtitles at the Anime Expo on July 4, 2019. It was released in Japan on July 12, 2019 and was released worldwide outside of Japan and Korea on Pokémon Day on February 27, 2020 on Netflix. It received a theatrical release in South Korea on September 30, 2020, and in mainland China on December 4, 2020. It was first revealed in a teaser trailer following M21 in Japan, which featured Mewtwo. The first official trailer was released on December 31, 2018.
trivia: This movie was released between SM129 and SM130 in Japan.

This movie is co-directed by Kunihiko Yuyama and Motonori Sakakibara, with the former returning after the previous movie was directed by Tetsuo Yajima. This subsequently makes this the first movie to be directed by two people as opposed to one.
Takeshi Shudō received a posthumous credit for this movie's screenplay.
The first poster for the movie is similar to the original teaser poster for Mewtwo Strikes Back.

This is one of two Pokémon-related movies to be released in 2019, with the other being the live action film, POKÉMON Detective Pikachu. Incidentally, both of them feature Mewtwo in a prominent role and heavily use CGI as opposed to 2D animation.

Just like the original movie, only Ash, Misty, Brock, Corey, Fergus, and Neesha successfully made it towards New Island. Unlike the original movie, which depicted only a female fourth Trainer takes off from the pier on the back of a Fearow (who still appears in this movie), several more Trainers are shown leaving Old Shore Wharf and headed towards New Island. Furthermore, unlike the original movie, where the subject wasn't mentioned, Ash and Misty directly mention the Trainers who didn't make it to the island, although their fates were still left unknown.
Unshō Ishizuka's narration is posthumously featured in this movie. It was recorded in March 2018.[9]

The laboratory where Mewtwo is born has a completely different design, with predominantly white colors.

Instead of the spiral staircase being positioned at the far end of the hall in front of the entrance to the arena, it is now in front of the front door. It also has two staircases forming a double helix instead of a single staircase like in the original.

Mewtwo's armor has a different design. It frequently moves along with Mewtwo in combat and can also act as a restraint should it rebel. Giovanni activates this feature before Mewtwo escapes the Team Rocket HQ, but it fails to stop Mewtwo.

Raymond's skin color is darkened and his hairstyle is changed to give him dreadlocks, while his coat, pants, and bandanna are altered to give him a more traditional pirate-like look. He is also given gloves, which he did not have in the original movie.

Ash's Charizard, Misty's Psyduck, and Brock's Vulpix all appear earlier in the movie, during the lunch scene.

Charizard is added into most of the scenes alongside Squirtle and Bulbasaur and responds positively to Ash in all of them. The original movie took place in conjunction with the animated series continuity, and therefore, Charizard would still be disobedient at the time. Those behaviors have been mostly erased in this movie, presumably to avoid confusion to newer viewers, with the closest thing to a hint at its original disobedient nature being Charizard preemptively trying to attack Dragonite and Mewtwo without Ash's permission.
Ash's Charizard attacks using Flamethrower on Dragonite when it lands.

Unlike the original movie, which depicted only a female fourth Trainer who takes off from the pier on the back of a Fearow (who still appears in this movie), two more Trainers are shown leaving Old Shore Wharf and headed towards New Island. Furthermore, unlike the original movie, where the subject wasn't mentioned, Ash and Misty directly mention the Trainers who didn't make it to the island, although their fates were still left unknown.
Misty reacts with excitement to Fergus' Vaporeon and other Water Pokémon, and she rushes to greet them until Gyarados emerges. An exchange between Ash and Fergus about Gyarados is also added.

Both Bruteroot and Shellshocker last longer in battle against the clone Venusaur and Blastoise. Bruteroot survives the initial Vine Whip attack and is knocked out by Leaf Storm, whereas Shellshocker is knocked out by the same Rapid Spin but after exchanging a head-on Skull Bash.
Nurse Joy gives information about Ash, Misty, and Brock before she asks if they need to be invited. Mewtwo is also clearly depicted in this scene, whereas in the original he is obscured.
Team Rocket attempts to take Ash and his friends to New Island in a Lapras-shaped sailboat, with the Viking motif being eliminated entirely. Team Rocket also sing a song during this scene.
Brock tries to flirt with Neesha and also notes his attraction to Miranda.
A number of moves that were introduced in later generations, such as Energy Ball and Leaf Storm, are used in this movie.
When Ash is petrified during the movie's climax, he turns to black stone instead of gray rock.
The ending credits now feature paintings of Ash and his friends in different areas.

A Generation III Pokémon, Wingull, appears in the movie's ending credits.
Miranda also mentions Wingull earlier in the movie. This is an alteration of an existing line in the Japanese version of Mewtwo Strikes Back, where she refers to regular seagulls instead.

The post-credits scene, which was previously a shot of Mew flying off into the mountains, now shows Mewtwo and the clones flying toward Mount Quena, foreshadowing Mewtwo Returns.

Some of the music featured in the movie is remixed from preceding movies, including Black—Victini and Reshiram, Genesect and the Legend Awakened (which also starred a Mewtwo), Hoopa and the Clash of Ages, and Volcanion and the Mechanical Marvel.

While the dialogue is largely unchanged between the Japanese versions of both movies, the dialogue in this movie's English dub is mostly not based on the original movie's dub script, save for a few select lines, and is instead re-translated to be closer to the Japanese versions' scripts.

Most of the 1990s era songs that play during the English dub of the movie, such as the Blessed Union of Souls song Brother My Brother (which played as Ash first saw the clones and originals fighting en masse), are omitted and replaced with the movie's score. The exception to this is the cover of the Pokémon Theme that plays during the battle with Raymond, which is a fresh cover.

The scene where Misty hides Togepi in her bag while Mewtwo is capturing the other Pokémon is made more obvious to the audience, as she tells it to "be very quiet in there". She also tells it to hide in her bag during the boat ride.
Psyduck is captured while hiding behind a pillar instead of when it is running away with Misty and Brock.
Nurse Joy and Brock try to open the door to escape, just before Vulpix is captured by Mewtwo.

When Jessie accidentally activates the Pokémon replication system, Dr. Fuji's voice is heard explaining how the machine works. However, in the original movie's English dub, a feminine robotic voice is heard, with Dr. Fuji's voice speaking about Mewtwo's creation after Meowth's DNA had been extracted.
Mew and Mewtwo don't use sphere barriers while they are attacking each other. However, their bodies respectively still emit pink and blue sparks while they attack each other.

Originally when Mewtwo catches Charizard, Bruteroot and Shellshocker, their respective Trainers were frozen in shock. In this remake, Ash leaps to try to get the Poké Ball back after Charizard is captured, while the other two Trainers try to block the Balls and then get them back.
While Mewtwo is catching everyone's Pokémon, Ash comes up with the idea to return them to their Poké Balls immediately, instead of suddenly coming up with the idea.
In the Czech dub, when Nurse Joy gives information about Ash, Misty, and Brock before she asks if they need to be invited, she introduces Brock as Misty's brother.

Although Mewtwo's conversation towards Dr. Fuji regarding the nature of Mewtwo's existence is translated faithfully from the Japanese version, the English dub replaces the reference to God with "nature" to omit any religious references.
Keep Evolving replaces Together With the Wind as the ending theme.

In the original Japanese version, when Brock tries to show love to Neesha, he mentions making rice balls. In the English dub, he calls them jelly doughnuts. This is likely a reference to the infamous dub edit from Primeape Goes Bananas.
The sequence of Pikachu transitioning from a 2D image in a game window to jumping out and becoming 3D was removed in the English dub.
In the original Japanese version, a researcher asks if Mew is a devil or an angel. In the English dub, he wonders if it is good or evil.
In the original Japanese version, Raymond mentions that Ash got eight Badges. This isn't mentioned in the English dub.
In the English dub, Nurse Joy implies that Ash, his friends, Neesha, Fergus, and Corey were invited. She doesn't make this implication in the original Japanese version.
In the original Japanese version, as the Pokémon cry, only Pikachu's voice is heard. In the English dub, all of the other Pokémon's voices are heard.

In total, ConceptLab has illustrated 10 cards (excluding reprints). A full list of cards illustrated by ConceptLab can be found here. ConceptLab was founded on February 20, 2017, and, as of April 26, 2024, it employs 70 people. ConceptLab works in areas such as video planning and production, commercial development, game development, 2D design, and illustration production.

Nishida's submitted illustration would be used as the art for her first card, Gardevoir, one of the SM-P Promotional cards. Beginning with Celebi from Shining Fates, Nishida has been illustrating cards on a regular basis. She also illustrated the booster pack artwork for VMAX Climax. Nishida has been drawing every day since she was young. She began illustrating professionally in 2017, and works part-time as an art teacher at the high school she attended in her youth. She currently uses a touchscreen tablet and Clip Studio Paint to produce her artwork. Nishida became a fan of the Pokémon franchise as a child, playing Pokémon FireRed and watching Jirachi: Wish Maker. Nishida's favorite generation is Generation V, and her favorite Pokémon is Yamask.[1]

name: Taiga Kasai
bio: Taiga Kasai (Japanese: カサイタイガ) is an artist for the Pokémon series. He was a participant in both the 2nd Pokémon Card Game Illustration Grand Prix and the Pokémon Trading Card Game Illustration Contest 2022 illustration contests, being the Japanese First Runner-up for the latter. According to Kasai, he begged his parents to buy him the tools to allow him to enter, as being an artist on the TCG had always been a dream of his.[1] Kasai's runner-up artwork would be used to create his first Pokémon card, Greninja, one of the SWSH Black Star Promos. When illustrating this artwork of Greninja, he carefully considered the contest's theme of how Pokémon would spend their days in the wild; seeing as Greninja is based on a ninja, he drew it as if it was planning a strategy for battle.[1] Kasai also confirmed that he drew many drafts for each individual Pokémon that was eligible for the contest, though he knew his idea for Greninja was the perfect fit from the very start.[1] That being said, Kasai admitted he struggled with the background of the piece, saying that his leading concern was making the subject stand out from the background itself.[1] It didn't start to sink in that he had won the award until he had received the physical copy of the Greninja card, and seeing the existing TCG artists that he looked up to congratulate him on Twitter after announcing that he had won the award was a huge moment for him.[1] He draws digitally, opting to use an iPad Pro.[1] He first began drawing after seeing a Pokémon illustration by his father, who was already an artist.[1] He didn't think of himself as particularly good, though decided to go to art school when taking the entrance exams for university, which was where he began studying how to draw.[1] Though Kasai first learned about Pokémon when he was in kindergarten through the stickers found on the series' branded Daiichi Pan, the first game he played was Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire, which also happen to be his favorites.[1] He first discovered the Pokémon Trading Card Game when sets were on sale at the theater when Kasai first watched M05, with his long-standing appeal for the game being as a result of its wealth of unique and talented illustrators.[1] In 2023, he made his debut as a game artist on Pokémon HOME and Pokémon GO. Kasai's favorite Pokémon is Aggron.[1]

name: MINAMINAMI Take
bio: MINAMINAMI Take (Japanese: 南波タケ) is a Saitama-based freelance illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Before working on the series in an official capacity, MINAMINAMI Take was a participant in the Pokémon Trading Card Game Illustration Contest 2022, where their submitted artwork of Arcanine was a semifinalist. Their first official card was Charmander, one of the SVP Black Star Promos.

name: nisimono
bio: nisimono is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first cards were Weedle, Kakuna, and Beedrill from the 151 expansion.

name: KG-2000
bio: KG-2000 (Japanese: こむぎこ2000 Komugiko2000; born December 8, 2000) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Thus far, KG-2000 has illustrated  1 card, which was Farfetch'd from the 151 expansion. A full list of cards illustrated by KG-2000 can be found here. In 2024, they were a key animator on the Pokémon Day 2024 video POKÉDANCE, and also designed the character dancing with the Sinnoh first partner Pokémon.[1]

They began their work on the series as an illustrator on the Pokémon Trading Card Game, thus far they have illustrated 2. Their first contribution to the Pokémon Franchise we're Staryu and Starmie from the 151 expansion. For a list of cards they have illustrated, go here.

name: Takumi Wada
bio: Takumi Wada (Japanese: 和田(わだ) 拓(たくみ) Wada Takumi; born 1983[1]) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. For the Pokémon Trading Card Game: Online Illustration Exhibition, which was accessible between August 10 and October 22, 2022, they illustrated three different cards specifically for the online exhibition. These cards were never physically distributed. Their first card to be printed was the Aegislash included in the Paradox Rift expansion. Besides working on the Pokémon TCG, Takumi Wada has been credited as the illustrator for The Legend of Zelda games Skyward Sword and Breath of the Wild.

name: USGMEN
bio: USGMEN (Japanese: うさぎメン Usagi-men) is a Japanese freelance artist for the Pokémon series, beginning as an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His first card was Mew ex from the Paldean Fates expansion. In 2024, he was a key animator on the Pokémon Day 2024 video POKÉDANCE, and also designed the character dancing with the Hoenn first partner Pokémon.[1] He also frequently posts animated Pokémon fan-art on his Twitter.

name: Kuroimori
bio: Kuroimori (Japanese: 黒イ森) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Gardevoir ex from the Paldean Fates expansion.

name: Dsuke
bio: Dsuke is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Chi-Yu, one of the SVP Black Star Promos.

name: Miranda Branley
bio: Miranda L. Branley is an American illustrator and designer for Pikachu Press at The Pokémon Company International who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. She has a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree from the Milwaukee Institute of Art and Design, having majored in Illustration and minored in Communication Design.[1] Her first card to be printed was Oddish, one of the SVP Black Star Promos, which she illustrated for the animated series Pokémon: Path to the Peak.

name: Uninori
bio: Uninori (Japanese: 雲丹海苔) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, their first work being published in 2024 with Grotle from the Temporal Forces expansion. As early as 2018, Uninori submitted various pieces to Pokémon's TCG Illustration Contests. Judging from posts on social media, Uninori is heavily inspired by a variety of artists, namely Pokémon's Ken Sugimori and Kagemaru Himeno, as well as Dragon Ball and Dragon Quest artist Akira Toriyama.[2] This inspiration is further reflected in their style for the TCG, which was described in a Pokémon.com article as evoking the art style of the manga and anime industries during the 1990s.[3] Uninori's favorite Trainer battle theme is from Johto.[4]

name: Rond
bio: Rond (Japanese: ろんど Rondo) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Before illustrating for the series in an official capacity, Rond was a participant in the Pokémon Trading Card Game Illustration Contest 2022, where their submitted artwork of Charizard won a Judges' Award. Rond's first official card was Deerling from the Temporal Forces expansion. Rond's art style involves use of soft lines and colors alongside blur effects.[1]

name: mingo
bio: mingo is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Before illustrating for the series in an official capacity, mingo was a participant in the Pokémon Trading Card Game Illustration Contest 2022, where their submitted artwork of Pikachu was a Second Runner-Up. mingo's first official card was Rabsca from the Temporal Forces expansion. mingo's art style involves heavy use of bright colors and vaporwave-esque backgrounds which accentuate the subject's personality.[1]

name: Saboteri
bio: Saboteri (Japanese: サボテリ) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Before working on the series in an official capacity, Saboteri (then credited as savoteri) was a participant in the Pokémon Trading Card Game Illustration Contest 2022, where their submitted artwork of Scizor was a semi-finalist. Their first official card was Squirtle from the Japanese Venusaur & Charizard & Blastoise Special Deck Set ex, which would later be included in the English Stellar Crown expansion. Saboteri's artwork debuted in English with the Temporal Forces expansion, which included Rellor and illustration rare Excadrill.

name: takashi shiraishi
bio: takashi shiraishi (Japanese: 白石貴士 Shiraishi Takashi; born May 10, 1986, in the Ehime Prefecture) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His first card was Ponyta from the Temporal Forces expansion. Most of takashi shiraishi's artwork uses acrylic paint. He also regularly showcases his artwork in exhibitions in different locations all over Japan.

name: Krgc
bio: Krgc or Koroguchi (born February 20) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Centiskorch from the Temporal Forces expansion.

name: Orca
bio: Orca is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Bulbasaur from the Japanese Venusaur & Charizard & Blastoise Special Deck Set ex, which is included in the English Stellar Crown expansion. Their first cards released in English were Snom and illustration rare Lickitung from the Temporal Forces expansion.

name: cochi8i
bio: cochi8i (Japanese: こちやい Kochiyai) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game, the first of which being Raichu from the Cyber Judge expansion. They draw digitally, opting to use Clip Studio Paint as their application of choice.[2] They claim to have drawn influence to their work from media they engaged with at a young age, citing Disney's Tarzan, A Bug's Life, as well as picture-books, such as Barbapapa and I'm Chihikkoshi as examples.[3]

name: Makura Tami
bio: Makura Tami (Japanese: まくらたみ) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Before working on the series in an official capacity, Makura Tami (then credited as TamiMakura) was a participant in the Pokémon Trading Card Game Illustration Contest 2022, where their submitted artwork of Bulbasaur was a semi-finalist. Their first official card was Azumarill from the Temporal Forces expansion.

name: Katsunori Sato
bio: Katsunori Sato (Japanese: 佐藤 勝則 Sato Katsunori) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Thus far, Katsunori Sato has illustrated 5 cards, the first of which was Bronzong from the Temporal Forces expansion. A full list of cards illustrated by Katsunori Sato can be found here.

bio: mele (Japanese: メレ; born December 4, 2000) is a freelance illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game.  Their first card was Duosion from the Temporal Forces expansion. Other than the Pokémon Trading Card Game, mele has contributed artwork for music videos for Japanese singers, for video games such as Overwatch or Project Sekai, and for VTuber agencies Hololive Production and Nijisanji.

name: Shimaris Yukichi
bio: Shimaris Yukichi (Japanese: しまりすゆきち Shimarisu Yukichi) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Ekans from the Temporal Forces expansion. Shimaris Yukichi typically illustrates cute, round Pokémon atop simple backgrounds.[1]

name: Minato
bio: Minato is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Thus far, Minato has illustrated 1 card, which was Arbok from the Temporal Forces expansion. A full list of cards illustrated by Minato can be found here.

name: osare
bio: osare is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Before illustrating for the series in an official capacity, osare was a participant in the Pokémon Trading Card Game Illustration Contest 2022, where their submitted artwork of Scizor was a quarter-finalist. osare's first official card was Forretress from the Temporal Forces expansion. osare has a cartoony art style, using heavy curves and disconnected lines in their work.[1]

name: toi8
bio: toi8 (born October 8) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Thus far, toi8 has illustrated 5 cards, the first of which was Noctowl from the Temporal Forces expansion. A full list of cards illustrated by toi8 can be found here. Before contributing artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game, he has worked on Tokyo Mirage Sessions ♯FE as a key artist, Fate/Grand Order as a character artist, and Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood as a background artist.
trivia: toi8 is Tomomi Ozaki's husband.[1]

name: GOTO minori
bio: GOTO minori (Japanese: ごとうみのり) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was Chatot from the Temporal Forces expansion.

name: Mékayu
bio: Mékayu (Japanese: めぇかゆ) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first cards were Pidove and illustration rare Drampa from the Temporal Forces expansion. Mékayu's art style has been described as having a storybook-like aesthetic.[1]

name: Susumu Maeya
bio: Susumu Maeya (Japanese: 前屋 進 Maeya Susumu) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Her first cards were illustration rare Deerling and Sawsbuck from the Temporal Forces expansion. Outside Pokémon, she is also the mangaka of The Food Diary of Miss Maid.

Other than the Pokémon Trading Card Game, danciao has designed Ivan the Terrible and Xiang Yu for Fate/Grand Order, and has also been a guest artist for Duel Masters Trading Card Game.

name: MARINA Chikazawa

name: Yukihiro Tada
bio: Yukihiro Tada (Japanese: タダユキヒロ Tada Yukihiro; born in Osaka) is a freelance illustrator and comic artist who has contributed artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His first card was illustration rare Pinsir from the Twilight Masquerade expansion. Yukihiro Tada graduated from the faculty of arts at Kyoto Seika University. He won the annual prize in The Choice held in 2005 by Genkosha, a publishing company, and also created illustrations for the official Japanese lyric video for 7 Years, a song by Lukas Graham nominated for three Grammys.[1] His illustrations for the TCG typically involve laidback environmental scenes.[2]

name: Yuriko Akase
bio: Yuriko Akase (Japanese: 赤瀬 由里子 Akase Yuriko; born 1990) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Their first card was illustration rare Timburr from the Twilight Masquerade expansion. Yuriko Akase typically illustrates their subject in a relaxed, slice-of-life scene.[1]

name: Kouichi Ooyama
bio: Kouichi Ooyama (Japanese: 大山 功一 Ōyama Kōichi), born 1960, is one of the original game designers of the Pokémon Trading Card Game, and later Pokémon Duel. He was also the illustrator for What's Nassy's Favorite Word? and worked on EarthBound as an art director, graphic designer, and game designer. He made a cameo in the Pokémon Trading Card Game video game as a Pokémon Card researcher, Dr. Ooyama (Dr. Mason in the English version of the game). Dr. Ooyama looks like Ooyama, but with gray hair, a lab coat, and a Pokémon Card attached to his head. Kouichi Ooyama has appeared at the Tropical Mega Battle in costume as Dr. Ooyama.
